Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥusayn and a throng of our companions narrated to him, who said that Abū’l-Ḥusayn ʿUbayd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. Jaʿfar al-Qaṣbānī narrated to them, saying that Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥusayn b. Wasīf al-ʿAdl narrated to him among others, who said that ʿAlī b. Yaʿqūb narrated to him among others, who said that ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad b. Maḥfūẓ b. al-Mubārak al-Anṣārī al-Balawī narrated to him among others, who said that Ibrāhīm b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ al-Madanī narrated to him among others, who said that Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥusayn narrated to him, and also he said that Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan b. Ḥamza al-ʿAlawī (ra) narrated to him among others, who said that Abū Ghānim Ismāʿīl b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Ḥārithī narrated to him among others, in Mecca, who said that Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-ʿAlawī narrated to him among others, who said that Ibrāhīm b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to him among others, as did Ḥamza b. Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Zayd b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib. They said that Abū’l-Ḥusayn Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn al-Daynūrī informed them, saying that Yaʿqūb b. Nuʿaym b. Qarqara narrated to him among others, saying that Jaʿfar b. Aḥmad b. ʿAbd al-Jabbār al-Sabīʿī narrated to him among others, in Medina, from his father, from Ibrāhīm b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ, who said that Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him, and that Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. Qulawayh narrated to him among others, saying that Abū ʿĪsā ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-Faḍl b. Muḥammad b. Hilāl al-Ṭāʾī narrated to him among others, saying that Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-ʿAlawī narrated to him among others, saying that Ibrāhīm b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to him among others, saying that Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him. She said: “When Abū’l-Dawānīq murdered ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥasan b. al-Ḥusayn after having murdered his two sons Muḥammad and Ibrāhīm…” And al-Sharīf Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Isḥāq b. al-Ḥusayn b. Isḥāq b. Mūsā b. Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib narrated to us, saying that Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. Ḥamza b. al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd al-Madīnī narrated to him among others, saying that his father narrated to him, who said that Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh b. Muḥammad al-Balawī narrated to him, saying that Ibrāhīm b. ʿUbayd Allāh b. al-ʿAlāʾ narrated to him among others, saying that Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥusayn narrated to him. She has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “When Abū’l-Dawānīq murdered ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Ḥasan b. al-Ḥusayn after having murdered his two sons Muḥammad and Ibrāhīm, he carried my son, Dāwūd b. al-Ḥusayn, from Medina to Iraq bound in irons along with the sons of his uncle from among the descendants of al-Ḥasan [al-Mujtabā]. Hence he had disappeared from me for some time, being there imprisoned, and all news of him had been cut off, and his whereabouts obscured. I had supplicated to Allāh and pleaded to Him, asking Him sincerely, and sought assistance from my brothers—who were among the worshipful, ascetics and people of diligence and effort—to supplicate to Allāh for my sake that my son and I may be reunited before my death. They did thus, without any shortcoming on their part, while rumour reached me that Dāwūd had been murdered. Others rejected that news and insisted that he had been walled up inside a cylinder with his cousins. My calamity thus became greater and my depression severer, and I did not see how my supplication would be answered or my issue would be resolved successfully. Thus, my bones became frail, my years increased and I became fed up to the point of losing hope that I would reunite with my child due to my weakness and the passing of my life.” Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥusayn continued: “Then I entered upon Abū ʿAbd Allāh, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), and he was ill. I asked him about his condition, and supplicated for him, and I was about to leave when he said: “O’ Umm Dāwūd, what has reached you (of news) about Dāwūd?”—and I had nursed Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad with the same milk with which I had nursed Dāwūd, so when he mentioned him I wept and said: “May I be sacrificed for your sake! Where is Dāwūd? He is (seeming to me) lost in Iraq, and I am totally cut off from any news of his whereabouts, having despaired of meeting him again, even though I still fervently seek to see him and yearn for him greatly, so I ask you to pray for him, for he is your milk brother.” Umm Dāwūd, Fāṭima bt. ʿAbd Allāh b. Ibrāhīm b. al-Ḥusayn, continued to narrate: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as) said to me: “O’ Umm Dāwūd, where are you with the supplication of openings, answers and success? [1] For it is the supplication by which Allāh (azwj) opens up the skies for the supplicant and the angels receive him with the glad tidings of a worthy answer (to his supplication). It is the answered supplication which is never hidden from Allāh (azwj), and what accompanies it with Allāh (twt) merits no reward less than Paradise.” Umm Dāwūd continues to narrate: “I said: “And how is that for me, o’ son of the pure, truthful ones?,” so Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad replied: “O’ Umm Dāwūd, indeed one of the sacred months is near”—and by this he (as) meant the month of Rajab—“and it is a blessed and exalted month of immense sanctity in which supplications are heard. Thus, I implore you to fast of it three days—the thirteenth, fourteenth and fifteenth—for these are the white days. On the 15th day—the middle one—perform the ritual bath (ghusl) at noontime and thereby perform eight units of prayer with attention and care, ennobling thereby each unit, prostration and supplication. In the first unit, recite the Opening Chapter of the Book (i.e. Sūrat al-Fātiḥa) and then ﴾Say, “O’ disbelievers,”﴿, and in the second unit ﴾Say, “He is Allāh, Who is One,”﴿, and then in the remaining six units recite whichever short chapters you prefer. Then perform the Ẓuhr prayer—thereafter perform eight more units with attention and care, ennobling thereby each unit, prostration and supplication. May you conduct your prayer in the most immaculate clothing and in a clean house, on a clean mat, and use perfume, for the angels love it. Put in effort to ensure that no-one enters upon you to distract you with their speech or actions”—the rest which we have not written down here has been mentioned in the book ʿAmal al-Sunna, [2] so whoever wishes to record it, let him do so from ʿAmal al-Sunna—“when you cease supplicating, prostrate on the ground, placing your cheeks on the ground and say: “To You I have prostrated and in You I have believed, so have mercy on me in my humiliation, my need, and the abasement of my face.” Make an effort to weep from your eyes, even if your tears are as small as the head of a fly, for this is the sign of the acceptance of this supplication—the burning of the heart and the shedding of tears. So, memorise what I teach you and beware that this supplication exit from your possession and come into the hands of another who supplicates using it without any right, for it is a noble prayer that contains the Greatest Name of Allāh which, if used, ensures that the supplication is answered and given—even if the heavens and the earth were closed off and all (the water of) the seas pooled together other than that and thereafter altogether stood between yourself and your need, Allāh (azwj) would make easy a way to that which you desire, and fulfil your request, judge well on your need, and validate your hopes. Every person who supplicates with this supplication will receive an answer from Allāh (taa), be they male or female. Even if the totality of mankind and the jinn were to unite as enemies of your child, Allāh would suffice for you against their provisions, silence their tongues against you and bend their necks low against you, if Allāh wills.” Umm Dāwūd continued to narrate: “He wrote for me this supplication and I returned to my residence wherein the month of Rajab arrived, so I observed the days by fasting and supplicating—as I was commanded—and at the end (of each day) I performed the Maghrib and ʿIshāʾ prayers, then broke my fast and then I performed the supererogatory night prayers of what was easy for me, arranged as I had my night. In my sleep (i.e. dream), I saw—as I had prayed for—the angels, the Prophets, the martyrs and the worshipful ones. I also saw the Holy Prophet (sawa), whereupon he said to me: “O’ daughter, o’ Umm Dāwūd, I come to you with good tidings, for every one of whom you have seen are your helpers, your brothers, and intercessors, and every one of them prays for your forgiveness and gives you the glad tidings of the successful fulfilment of your wish. I personally give you the glad tidings of forgiveness from Allāh and His satisfaction—rejoice in the goodness you have been rewarded with. I bear you glad tidings that Allāh has kept your son alive and will return him to you, if Allāh wills.” Umm Dāwūd continued to narrate: “I woke up from my sleep, and by Allāh, only a measure of time equivalent to the quick journey of a rider on the road from Iraq had passed when Dāwūd appeared before me and said: “O’ my mother, indeed I have been imprisoned in Iraq in the most claustrophobic kind of imprisonment, laden with heavy irons. I was in the condition of Ilyās (i.e. despair) concerning release when, on the night of the 15th of Rajab, I slept and dreamt that I saw the whole world. It had been lowered for me until I noticed you, praying on a mat, surrounded by men whose heads were in the sky and whose feet planted firmly on the ground, robed in green, glorifying Allāh around you. One of them spoke up, whose face was as beautiful and sweet as that of the Holy Prophet (sawa), whose robes were clean and whose scent was sublime, and excellent was his speech, whereupon he said: “O’ son of the righteous woman, rejoice in glad tidings, for Allāh (azwj) has answered your mother’s supplication!” It was thus that I woke up and a messenger of Abī’l-Dawānīq took me to see him during the night. He ordered my irons removed and had me treated with kindness, gave me ten thousand dirhams and freed me, having me carried on a camel that travelled at the most notable speed. Thus, I hastened until I entered Medina.” Umm Dāwūd narrates: “Immediately I took him to see Abī ʿAbd Allāh, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), so he greeted Dāwūd with greetings of peace, and had a pleasant conversation with him, until he—al-Ṣādiq—told Dāwūd: “Indeed, Abāʿl-Dawānīq saw ʿAlī (as) in a dream, who said to him: “Release my descendant, or I will cast you into the Fire!” Abū’l-Dawānīq then saw that there were fires blazing beneath his feet (in the dream). He woke up in a fit of helpless terror, so he let you go.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Rajab
chapter: The Tradition of Umm Dāwūd and Her Deed of Worship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Abū Muḥammad Jaʿfar b. Nuʿaym al-Ḥājim narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, who said that Ismāʿīl b. Mihrān narrated to him among others, as did ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Warrāq. The latter said that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from al-Haytham b. Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, who said that Ismāʿīl b. Mihrān narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Yazīd, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said that Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad narrated to him, from his father, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī (Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir), from his father, ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, from his father, al-Ḥusayn, from his brother, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, from their father, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), who said: “Whoever fasts a day of Rajab, whether it be at the month’s beginning, its middle, or its end, will have what he brought forth of his sins forgiven, as well as what he has kept back. Whoever fasts three days of Rajab at the month’s beginning, three days in its middle, and three at its end, will have what he brought forth of his sins forgiven, as well as what he has kept back. Whoever stays awake (engaged in prayer) during one of the nights of Rajab will receive his freedom from the Fire from Allāh, and his intercession for seventy thousand sinners is accepted. Whoever gives charity in the form of ṣadaqa in the month of Rajab seeking the Face (i.e. satisfaction) of Allāh, will be honoured by Allāh on the Day of Judgement in Paradise with a reward that no eyes have seen, nor any ear heard, nor any human intellect has grasped.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبو محمد جعفر بن نعيم الحاجم، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن إدريس، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطّاب، قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن مهران، وحدثنا علي بن عبد الله الورّاق، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، عن الهيثم بن أبي مسروق النهدي، قال: حدثنا إسماعيل بن مهران، عن محمد بن يزيد، عن سفيان الثوري، قال: حدثني جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه محمد بن علي، عن أبيه علي بن الحسين، عن أبيه الحسين، عن أخيه الحسن بن علي، عن علي بن أبي طالب (عليهم السلام)، قال: من صام يوماً من رجب في أوله أو في وسطه أو في آخره غفر له ما تقدم ذنبه وما تأخر، ومن صام ثلاثة أيام من رجب في أوله وثلاثة أيام في وسطه وثلاثة أيام في آخره غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، ومن أحيى ليلة من ليالي رجب أعتقه الله من النار وقبل شفاعته في سبعين الف رجل من المذنبين، ومن تصدق بصدقة في رجب ابتغاء وجه الله أكرمه الله يوم القيامة في الجنة من الثواب ما لا عين رأت ولا أذن سمعت ولا خطر على قلب بشر.
thaqalaynSanad: Abū Muḥammad Jaʿfar b. Nuʿaym al-Ḥājim narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, who said that Ismāʿīl b. Mihrān narrated to him among others, as did ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Warrāq. The latter said that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from al-Haytham b. Abī Masrūq al-Nahdī, who said that Ismāʿīl b. Mihrān narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Yazīd, from Sufyān al-Thawrī, who said that Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad narrated to him, from his father, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī (Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir), from his father, ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, from his father, al-Ḥusayn, from his brother, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī, from their father, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasts a day of Rajab, whether it be at the month’s beginning, its middle, or its end, will have what he brought forth of his sins forgiven, as well as what he has kept back. Whoever fasts three days of Rajab at the month’s beginning, three days in its middle, and three at its end, will have what he brought forth of his sins forgiven, as well as what he has kept back. Whoever stays awake (engaged in prayer) during one of the nights of Rajab will receive his freedom from the Fire from Allāh, and his intercession for seventy thousand sinners is accepted. Whoever gives charity in the form of ṣadaqa in the month of Rajab seeking the Face (i.e. satisfaction) of Allāh, will be honoured by Allāh on the Day of Judgement in Paradise with a reward that no eyes have seen, nor any ear heard, nor any human intellect has grasped.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Rajab
chapter: The Tradition of Umm Dāwūd and Her Deed of Worship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿImrān al-Daqqāq narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, saying that Mūsā b. ʿImrān al-Nakhʿī narrated to him among others, from his paternal uncle, al-Ḥusayn b. Yazīd al-Nawfalī, saying that he heard Mālik b. Anas, the jurist, who said: “By Allāh! I have not seen with mine own eyes anyone more virtuous than Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), ascetic and impeccable, worshipful and pious, and when I intended (to invite) him (to meet with me), he would graciously accept. One day, I asked him: “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is the reward for one who fasts a day of the month of Rajab, faithfully and having taken account?” He said—and by Allāh, when he spoke he was truthful: “My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who has stated that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said: “Whoever fasts a day of the month of Rajab, faithfully and having taken account, will be forgiven.” I then asked him: “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is the reward for one who fasts a day of the month of Shaʿbān, faithfully and having taken account?,” so Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad replied: “My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who has stated that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said: “Whoever fasts a day of the month of Shaʿbān, faithfully and having taken account, will be forgiven.”
arabicText: حدثنا علي بن أحمد بن محمد بن عمران الدقّاق، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أبي عبد الله الكوفي، قال: حدثنا موسى بن عمران النخعي، عن عمه الحسين بن يزيد النوفلي، قال: سمعت مالك بن أنس الفقيه يقول: والله ما رأت عيني أفضل من جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام) زهداً وفضلاً وعبادة وورعاً، فكنت أقصده فيكرمني ويقبل علي، فقلت له يوماً: يا ابن رسول الله ما ثواب من صام يوماً من رجب إيماناً وإحتساباً؟ قال—وكان والله إذا قال صدق—: حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): من صام يوماً من رجب إيماناً وإحتساباً غفر له، فقلت له: يا ابن رسول الله فما ثواب من صام يوماً من شعبان؟ قال: حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن جده، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): من صام يوماً من شعبان إيماناً وإحتساباً غفر له.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿImrān al-Daqqāq narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, saying that Mūsā b. ʿImrān al-Nakhʿī narrated to him among others, from his paternal uncle, al-Ḥusayn b. Yazīd al-Nawfalī, saying that he heard Mālik b. Anas, the jurist, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “By Allāh! I have not seen with mine own eyes anyone more virtuous than Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), ascetic and impeccable, worshipful and pious, and when I intended (to invite) him (to meet with me), he would graciously accept. One day, I asked him: “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is the reward for one who fasts a day of the month of Rajab, faithfully and having taken account?” He said—and by Allāh, when he spoke he was truthful: “My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who has stated that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said: “Whoever fasts a day of the month of Rajab, faithfully and having taken account, will be forgiven.” I then asked him: “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is the reward for one who fasts a day of the month of Shaʿbān, faithfully and having taken account?,” so Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad replied: “My father narrated to me, from his father, from his grandfather, who has stated that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said: “Whoever fasts a day of the month of Shaʿbān, faithfully and having taken account, will be forgiven.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Rajab
chapter: The Tradition of Umm Dāwūd and Her Deed of Worship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbdūs al-Nīshābūrī al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Qutayba al-Nīshābūrī narrated to him among others, saying that Ḥamdān b. Sulaymān narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. Nuʿmān narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭāʾī narrated to him among others, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d), who said: “Whoever fasts on the twenty-seventh of Rajab will have recorded for him the reward of fasting for seventy years.”
arabicText: حدثنا عبد الواحد بن محمد بن عبدوس النيشابوري العطّار، قال: حدثنا علي بن محمد بن قتيبة النيشابوري، قال: حدثنا حمدان بن سليمان، قال: حدثنا علي بن نعمان، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن طائي، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليهما السلام)، قال: من صام سبعة وعشرين من رجب كتب له أجر صيام سبعين سنة.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Muḥammad b. ʿAbdūs al-Nīshābūrī al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. Qutayba al-Nīshābūrī narrated to him among others, saying that Ḥamdān b. Sulaymān narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. Nuʿmān narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭāʾī narrated to him among others, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasts on the twenty-seventh of Rajab will have recorded for him the reward of fasting for seventy years.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Rajab
chapter: The Tradition of Umm Dāwūd and Her Deed of Worship
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Tamīm al-Qazwīnī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Anṣārī narrated to him among others, from ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ṣāliḥ al-Harawī, saying that ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) has stated: “Whoever fasts the first day of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts two days of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts three days of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him, and satisfied with him, as his enemies would also be, on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts seven days of Rajab will have the doors of the heavens and the earth—seven each, respectively—opened up for his spirit when he dies until it reaches the loftiest realms (of existence). Whoever fasts eight days of Rajab will have all eight doors of Paradise opened for him. Whoever fasts fifteen days of Rajab will have Allāh (azwj) grant him every wish of his except that which involves sin or cutting ties with one’s kin. Whoever fasts the whole month of Rajab will be absolved from his sins as if he were as innocent as on the day his mother birthed him, and he will be freed from the Fire and admitted into Heaven to reside therein with the chosen, selected few.”
arabicText: حدثنا عثمان بن عبد الله بن تميم القزويني، قال: حدثنا أبي، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن علي الأنصاري، عن عبد السلام بن صالح الهروي، قال: قال علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام): من صام أول يوم من رجب رضي الله عنه يوم يلقاه، ومن صام يومين من رجب رضي الله عنه يوم يلقاه، ومن صام ثلاثة أيام من رجب رضي الله عنه وأرضاه وأرضى عنه خصمائه يوم يلقاه، ومن صام سبعة أيام من رجب فتحت أبواب السماوات السبع بروحه إذا مات حتى يصل إلى الملكوت الأعلى، ومن صام ثمانية أيام من رجب فتحت له أبواب الجنة الثمانية، ومن صام من رجب خمسة عشر يوماً قضى الله عز وجل له كل حاجة إلا أن يسأله في مأثم أو في قطيعة رحم، ومن صام شهر رجب كله خرج من ذنوبه كيوم ولدته أمه واعتق من النار وأدخل الجنة مع المصطفين الأخيار.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Tamīm al-Qazwīnī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Anṣārī narrated to him among others, from ʿAbd al-Salām b. Ṣāliḥ al-Harawī, saying that ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) has stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasts the first day of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts two days of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts three days of Rajab will have Allāh pleased with him, and satisfied with him, as his enemies would also be, on the day he meets Him. Whoever fasts seven days of Rajab will have the doors of the heavens and the earth—seven each, respectively—opened up for his spirit when he dies until it reaches the loftiest realms (of existence). Whoever fasts eight days of Rajab will have all eight doors of Paradise opened for him. Whoever fasts fifteen days of Rajab will have Allāh (azwj) grant him every wish of his except that which involves sin or cutting ties with one’s kin. Whoever fasts the whole month of Rajab will be absolved from his sins as if he were as innocent as on the day his mother birthed him, and he will be freed from the Fire and admitted into Heaven to reside therein with the chosen, selected few.”

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: The elder and jurist, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. Bābuwayh (ra) informed us, saying that his father (rh) narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Idrīs, who said that Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd narrated to him among others, from Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Faḍl al-Hāshimī, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d), who has stated: “Fasting in the month of Ramaḍān is a treasure for a servant (of Allāh) on the Day of Reckoning. But there is no such servant who fasts aplenty in Shaʿbān except that Allāh does right by his affairs of living and suffices for him against his enemies. The least of that which is given to him for his fasting for a day of Shaʿbān is that his admission into Paradise is mandatory.”
arabicText: أخبرنا الشيخ الفقيه أبو جعفر محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن بابويه رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله عن أحمد بن إدريس، قال: حدثنا محمد بن عيسى بن عبيد، عن يونس بن عبد الرحمن، عن عبد الله بن فضل الهاشمي، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليهما السلام)، قال: صيام شهر رمضان ذخر للعبد يوم القيامة، وما من عبد يكثر الصيام في شعبان إلا أصلح الله أمر معيشته، وكفاه شر عدوه وإن أدنى ما يكون لمن يصوم يوماً من شعبان أن تجب له الجنة.
thaqalaynSanad: The elder and jurist, Abū Jaʿfar Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. Bābuwayh (ra) informed us, saying that his father (rh) narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Idrīs, who said that Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā b. ʿUbayd narrated to him among others, from Yūnus b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Faḍl al-Hāshimī, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as-d), who has stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Fasting in the month of Ramaḍān is a treasure for a servant (of Allāh) on the Day of Reckoning. But there is no such servant who fasts aplenty in Shaʿbān except that Allāh does right by his affairs of living and suffices for him against his enemies. The least of that which is given to him for his fasting for a day of Shaʿbān is that his admission into Paradise is mandatory.”

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from Naṣr b. Muzāḥim, from Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Masʿūdī, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. Yazīd al-ʿUranī, who said that al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), has said that his father narrated to him, from his father, from his grandfather (as-p), who transmitted that which the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated: “Shaʿbān is my month, and the month of Ramaḍān is the month of Allāh. Whoever fasts a day of my month will earn the right of intercession on the Day of Reckoning. Whoever fasts two days of my month will be forgiven by Allāh of his sins, whatever he brought forward and whatever he kept back. Whoever fasts three days of my month will be told, “Begin anew with your actions.” Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, keeping his private parts and his speech from sin and refraining from harming others, will be forgiven by Allāh of his sins, whatever he brought forward and whatever he kept back, and Allāh will also free him from the Fire, make his residence in the Abode of Eternity possible, and accept his intercession for as many sinful monotheists as there are grains of sand in the desert of ʿĀlij.” [1]
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أبي القاسم، عن محمد بن علي الكوفي، عن نصر بن مزاحم، عن أبي عبد الرحمن المسعودي، عن العلاء بن يزيد العرني، قال: قال الصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام): حدثني أبي، عن أبيه، عن جده (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): شعبان شهري وشهر رمضان شهر الله فمن صام يوماً من شهري كنت شفيعه يوم القيامة، ومن صام يومين من شهري غفر الله له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، ومن صام ثلاثة أيام من شهري قيل له استأنف العمل، ومن صام شهر رمضان يحفظ فرجه ولسانه وكف أذاه عن الناس غفر الله له ذنوبه ما تقدم منها وما تأخر وأعتقه من النار وأحله دار القرار، وقبل شفاعته في عدد رمل عالج من مذنبي أهل التوحيد.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Kūfī, from Naṣr b. Muzāḥim, from Abī ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Masʿūdī, from al-ʿAlāʾ b. Yazīd al-ʿUranī, who said that al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), has said that his father narrated to him, from his father, from his grandfather (as-p), who transmitted that which the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Shaʿbān is my month, and the month of Ramaḍān is the month of Allāh. Whoever fasts a day of my month will earn the right of intercession on the Day of Reckoning. Whoever fasts two days of my month will be forgiven by Allāh of his sins, whatever he brought forward and whatever he kept back. Whoever fasts three days of my month will be told, “Begin anew with your actions.” Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, keeping his private parts and his speech from sin and refraining from harming others, will be forgiven by Allāh of his sins, whatever he brought forward and whatever he kept back, and Allāh will also free him from the Fire, make his residence in the Abode of Eternity possible, and accept his intercession for as many sinful monotheists as there are grains of sand in the desert of ʿĀlij.” [1]

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl informed him among others, from his father, who said that he heard ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as-d) saying: “Whoever seeks the forgiveness of Allāh (twt) seventy times in Shaʿbān, Allāh will forgive him for his sins even if they number the count of the stars.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن إسحاق الطالقاني، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد الهمداني، قال: أخبرنا علي بن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن أبيه، قال: سمعت علي بن موسى الرضا (عليهما السلام) يقول: من استغفر الله تبارك وتعالى في شعبان سبعين مرة غفر الله ذنوبه ولو كانت مثل عدد النجوم.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Ṭāliqānī narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl informed him among others, from his father, who said that he heard ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as-d) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever seeks the forgiveness of Allāh (twt) seventy times in Shaʿbān, Allāh will forgive him for his sins even if they number the count of the stars.”

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl said: “I asked ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) about the fifteenth night of Shaʿbān, so he stated: “It is the night in which Allāh frees the necks from the Fire and forgives the sins (of the people who commit good deeds in it).” I asked him: “Is there any prayer to be performed on this night as opposed to the others?” The Imam replied: “There is nothing obligatory to perform in it, but if you want to perform something, then upon you is the prayer of Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib, [1] and increase in it mention of Allāh (azwj) and the supplication of forgiveness, for my father used to say: “It is the supplication that is answered inevitably.” I asked him: “Indeed, people say that this is the Night of Decree,” to which Imam al-Riḍā responded: “That is the Night of Power in the month of Ramaḍān.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: سألت علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام) عن ليلة النصف من شعبان قال: هي ليلة يعتق الله فيها الرقاب من النار ويغفر الذنوب فيها، قلت: هل جعل فيها صلاة زيادة على سائر الليالي؟ فقال: ليس فيها شئ موظف ولكن إن أحببت أن تطوع فيها بشئ فعليك بصلاة جعفر بن أبي طالب، وأكثر فيها من ذكر الله عز وجل، ومن الاستغفار والدعاء فإن أبي (عليه السلام) كان يقول: الدعاء فيها مستجاب، قلت له: إن الناس يقولون إنها ليلة الصكاك. فقال (عليه السلام): تلك ليلة القدر في شهر رمضان.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl said: “I asked ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) about the fifteenth night of Shaʿbān, so he stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “It is the night in which Allāh frees the necks from the Fire and forgives the sins (of the people who commit good deeds in it).” I asked him: “Is there any prayer to be performed on this night as opposed to the others?” The Imam replied: “There is nothing obligatory to perform in it, but if you want to perform something, then upon you is the prayer of Jaʿfar b. Abī Ṭālib, [1] and increase in it mention of Allāh (azwj) and the supplication of forgiveness, for my father used to say: “It is the supplication that is answered inevitably.” I asked him: “Indeed, people say that this is the Night of Decree,” to which Imam al-Riḍā responded: “That is the Night of Power in the month of Ramaḍān.”

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Aḥmad al-Maʿādī narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn narrated to him among others, saying that Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad al-Marwī narrated to him among others, from his father, from Yaḥyā b. ʿAbbās, saying that ʿAlī b. ʿĀṣim al-Wāsiṭī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAṭāʾ b. al-Sāʾib informed him, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) stated, while the merits of Shaʿbān were being mentioned in his presence: “It is an honourable month, and it is my month. The angels who carry the Throne exalt it and recognise its right, and it is the month in which the sustenance of the believers is increased, and it is the month of action in which the value of good deeds is doubled seventy times over and that of misdeeds is demolished, sins are forgiven, and good deeds are accepted. The Compeller—Allāh (jj)—acclaims His servants for their fasting and their fast-keeping, their prayers and their standing in worship as He looks on at them, acclaiming them before the carriers of the Throne.” ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as) stood up and exclaimed: “May my father and my mother be sacrificed for your sake, o’ Messenger of Allāh! I bid that you describe something of the merits of this month so that our desire to fast and stand in worship would be increased therein and our exertion of effort for the sake of the Glorious (azwj)!” The Prophet (sawa) obliged his request: “Whoever fasts the first day of Shaʿbān will have seventy good deeds recorded for him by Allāh, equivalent to the worship of a year. Whoever fasts two days of Shaʿbān will have his cardinal sins nullified. Whoever fasts three days of Shaʿbān will have seventy levels of the Paradisiacal realms raised for him, made of rubies and pearls. Whoever fasts four days of Shaʿbān will have his means of sustenance expanded. Whoever fasts five days of Shaʿbān will be beloved to the servants (of Allāh). Whoever fasts six days of Shaʿbān will have seventy kinds of affliction lifted from him. Whoever fasts seven days of Shaʿbān will be protected from Iblīs and his thralls for the rest of his worldly life. Whoever fasts eight days of Shaʿbān will not be excised from the world until his thirst is quenched with (a drink from) the Sanctified Basins. Whoever fasts nine days of Shaʿbān will be treated with kindness by Munkar and Nakīr when they interrogate him. Whoever fasts ten days of Shaʿbān will have the space of his grave widened by Allāh, by seventy cubits. Whoever fasts eleven days of Shaʿbān will have eleven rays of light shine upon his grave. Whoever fasts twelve days of Shaʿbān will have his grave be visited every day by seventy thousand angels until the Horn is blown (signifying the impending Resurrection). Whoever fasts thirteen days of Shaʿbān will have the angels of the seven Heavens supplicating for his forgiveness. Whoever fasts fourteen days of Shaʿbān will have all the animals and beasts, even the fish in the seas, praying for his forgiveness. Whoever fasts fifteen days of Shaʿbān will receive a call from the Lord of Honour as thus: “I will not burn you in the Fire!” Whoever fasts sixteen days of Shaʿbān will be saved from (being thrown into) seventy lakes of fire. Whoever fasts seventeen days of Shaʿbān will have the gates of Perdition shut to him, all of them. Whoever fasts eighteen days of Shaʿbān will have the gates of Paradise opened for him, all of them. Whoever fasts nineteen days of Shaʿbān will be given seventy thousand palaces made of pearls and sapphires in Heaven. Whoever fasts twenty days of Shaʿbān will be given seventy thousand wives from among the celestial maidens (ḥūr al-ʿayn). Whoever fasts twenty-one days of Shaʿbān will be welcomed by the angels, who shall caress him with their wings. Whoever fasts twenty-two days of Shaʿbān will be dressed in seventy bolts of silk and brocade. Whoever fasts twenty-three days of Shaʿbān will be given a saddled beast made of light when (or at the time) he emerges from his grave, then he will fly upon it to Heaven. Whoever fasts twenty-four days of Shaʿbān will be exonerated from the mere association with hypocrisy. Whoever fasts twenty-five days of Shaʿbān will be allowed to intercede for seventy thousand monotheists. Whoever fasts twenty-six days of Shaʿbān will have Allāh write for him a means of easy passage over the Bridge. Whoever fasts twenty-seven days of Shaʿbān will have a warrant of exoneration from Perdition written for him. Whoever fasts twenty-eight days of Shaʿbān will arrive on the Day of Reckoning with a face radiating like the moon. Whoever fasts twenty-nine days of Shaʿbān will attain the greatest satisfaction of Allāh. Whoever fasts thirty days of Shaʿbān will be the recipient of an exclamation from Jibraʾīl at the foot of the Throne as thus: “O’ person, begin anew your deeds, for you have been wholly forgiven for whatever has passed and had been brought forth of your sins!” The Most Glorious—Allāh (azwj)—will then say: “Had your sins been as numerous, even, as the stars in the sky, the raindrops in downpours, the leaves of trees, and the grains of sand, and riches, and the days of the world, you have been forgiven for all of them, and that is not in the least difficult for Allāh after what you have fasted in the month of Shaʿbān!” Ibn ʿAbbās made one last comment: “And this is all for the month of Shaʿbān.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن أحمد المعادي، قال: حدثنا محمد بن الحسين، قال: حدثنا أبو الحسن علي بن محمد بن علي، قال: حدثنا الحسن بن محمد المروي، عن أبيه، عن يحيى بن عبّاس، قال: حدثنا علي بن عاصم الواسطي، قال: أخبرني عطاء بن السائب، عن سعيد بن جبير، عن ابن عبّاس، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) وقد تذاكروا عنده فضائل شعبان، فقال: شهر شريف وهو شهري وحملة العرش تعظمه وتعرف حقه وهو شهر يزاد فيه أرزاق المؤمنين وهو شهر العمل فيه يضاعف الحسنة بسبعين والسيئة محطوطة والذنب مغفور والحسنة مقبولة والجبار جل جلاله يباهي فيه بعباده وينظر إلى صيامه وصوامه وقوامه وقيامه فيباهي به حملة العرش. فقام علي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام)، فقال: بأبي أنت وأمي يا رسول الله صف لنا شيئاً من فضائله لتزداد رغبة في صيامه وقيامه ولنجتهد للجليل عز وجل فيه، فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله): من صام أول يوم من شعبان كتب الله له سبعين حسنة تعدل عبادة سنة، ومن صام يومين من شعبان حطت عنه السيئة الموبقة، ومن صام ثلاثة أيام من شعبان رفع له سبعين درجة في الجنان من در وياقوت، ومن صام أربعة من شعبان وسع عليه في الرزق، ومن صام خمسة أيام من شعبان حبب إلى العباد، ومن صام ستة أيام من شعبان صرف عنه سبعون لونا من البلاء، ومن صام سبعة أيام من شعبان عصم من إبليس وجنوده دهر وعمره، ومن صام ثمانية أيام من شعبان لم يخرج من الدنيا حتى يسقى من حياض القدس، ومن صام تسعة أيام من شعبان عطف عليه منكر ونكير عندما يسألانه، ومن صام عشرة أيام من شعبان وسع الله عليه قبره سبعين ذراعاً، ومن صام أحد عشر يوماً من شعبان ضرب على قبره إحدى عشرة منارة من نور، ومن صام اثنى عشر يوماً من شعبان زاره في قبره كل يوم سبعون الف ملك إلى النفخ في الصور، ومن صام ثلاثة عشر يوماً من شعبان استغفرت له ملائكة سبع سماوات، ومن صام أربعة عشر يوماً من شعبان ألهمت الدواب والسباع حتى الحيتان في البحور أن يستغفروا له، ومن صام خمسة عشر يوماً من شعبان ناداه رب العزة لا أحرقك بالنار، ومن صام ستة عشر يوماً من شعبان أطفئ عنه سبعون بحراً من النيران، ومن صام سبعة عشر يوماً من شعبان أغلقت عنه أبواب النيران كلها، ومن صام ثمانية عشر يوماً من شعبان فتحت له أبواب الجنان كلها، ومن صام تسعة عشر يوماً من شعبان أعطى سبعين الف قصر من الجنان من در وياقوت، ومن صام عشرين يوماً من شعبان زوج سبعين الف زوجة من الحور العين، ومن صام أحد وعشرين يوماً من شعبان رحبت له الملائكة ومسحته بأجنحتها، ومن صام اثنين وعشرين يوماً من شعبان كسي سبعين حلة من سندس وإستبرق، ومن صام ثلاثة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان أتي بدابة من نور حين [عند خ ل] خروجه من قبره فيركبها طياراً إلى الجنة، ومن صام أربعة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان أعطي براءة من النفاق، ومن صام خمسة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان شفع في سبعين الف من أهل توحيد، ومن صام ستة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان كتب الله له جوازاً على الصراط، ومن صام سبعة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان كتب له براءة من النار، ومن صام ثمانية وعشرين يوماً من شعبان يهلل وجهه يوم القيامة، ومن صام تسعة وعشرين يوماً من شعبان نال رضوان الله الأكبر، ومن صام ثلاثين يوماً من شعبان ناداه جبرئيل من قدام العرش: يا هذا استأنف العمل عملاً جديداً فقد غفر لك ما مضى وتقدم من ذنوبك، والجليل عز وجل يقول: لو كان ذنوبك عدد نجوم السماء وقطر الأمطار وورق الأشجار وعدد الرمل والثرى وأيام الدنيا لغفرتها لك وما ذلك على الله بعزيز بعد صيامك شهر شعبان .قال ابن عبّاس: هذا لشهر شعبان.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Aḥmad al-Maʿādī narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn narrated to him among others, saying that Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad al-Marwī narrated to him among others, from his father, from Yaḥyā b. ʿAbbās, saying that ʿAlī b. ʿĀṣim al-Wāsiṭī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAṭāʾ b. al-Sāʾib informed him, from Saʿīd b. Jubayr, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) stated, while the merits of Shaʿbān were being mentioned in his presence:
thaqalaynMatn: “It is an honourable month, and it is my month. The angels who carry the Throne exalt it and recognise its right, and it is the month in which the sustenance of the believers is increased, and it is the month of action in which the value of good deeds is doubled seventy times over and that of misdeeds is demolished, sins are forgiven, and good deeds are accepted. The Compeller—Allāh (jj)—acclaims His servants for their fasting and their fast-keeping, their prayers and their standing in worship as He looks on at them, acclaiming them before the carriers of the Throne.” ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as) stood up and exclaimed: “May my father and my mother be sacrificed for your sake, o’ Messenger of Allāh! I bid that you describe something of the merits of this month so that our desire to fast and stand in worship would be increased therein and our exertion of effort for the sake of the Glorious (azwj)!” The Prophet (sawa) obliged his request: “Whoever fasts the first day of Shaʿbān will have seventy good deeds recorded for him by Allāh, equivalent to the worship of a year. Whoever fasts two days of Shaʿbān will have his cardinal sins nullified. Whoever fasts three days of Shaʿbān will have seventy levels of the Paradisiacal realms raised for him, made of rubies and pearls. Whoever fasts four days of Shaʿbān will have his means of sustenance expanded. Whoever fasts five days of Shaʿbān will be beloved to the servants (of Allāh). Whoever fasts six days of Shaʿbān will have seventy kinds of affliction lifted from him. Whoever fasts seven days of Shaʿbān will be protected from Iblīs and his thralls for the rest of his worldly life. Whoever fasts eight days of Shaʿbān will not be excised from the world until his thirst is quenched with (a drink from) the Sanctified Basins. Whoever fasts nine days of Shaʿbān will be treated with kindness by Munkar and Nakīr when they interrogate him. Whoever fasts ten days of Shaʿbān will have the space of his grave widened by Allāh, by seventy cubits. Whoever fasts eleven days of Shaʿbān will have eleven rays of light shine upon his grave. Whoever fasts twelve days of Shaʿbān will have his grave be visited every day by seventy thousand angels until the Horn is blown (signifying the impending Resurrection). Whoever fasts thirteen days of Shaʿbān will have the angels of the seven Heavens supplicating for his forgiveness. Whoever fasts fourteen days of Shaʿbān will have all the animals and beasts, even the fish in the seas, praying for his forgiveness. Whoever fasts fifteen days of Shaʿbān will receive a call from the Lord of Honour as thus: “I will not burn you in the Fire!” Whoever fasts sixteen days of Shaʿbān will be saved from (being thrown into) seventy lakes of fire. Whoever fasts seventeen days of Shaʿbān will have the gates of Perdition shut to him, all of them. Whoever fasts eighteen days of Shaʿbān will have the gates of Paradise opened for him, all of them. Whoever fasts nineteen days of Shaʿbān will be given seventy thousand palaces made of pearls and sapphires in Heaven. Whoever fasts twenty days of Shaʿbān will be given seventy thousand wives from among the celestial maidens (ḥūr al-ʿayn). Whoever fasts twenty-one days of Shaʿbān will be welcomed by the angels, who shall caress him with their wings. Whoever fasts twenty-two days of Shaʿbān will be dressed in seventy bolts of silk and brocade. Whoever fasts twenty-three days of Shaʿbān will be given a saddled beast made of light when (or at the time) he emerges from his grave, then he will fly upon it to Heaven. Whoever fasts twenty-four days of Shaʿbān will be exonerated from the mere association with hypocrisy. Whoever fasts twenty-five days of Shaʿbān will be allowed to intercede for seventy thousand monotheists. Whoever fasts twenty-six days of Shaʿbān will have Allāh write for him a means of easy passage over the Bridge. Whoever fasts twenty-seven days of Shaʿbān will have a warrant of exoneration from Perdition written for him. Whoever fasts twenty-eight days of Shaʿbān will arrive on the Day of Reckoning with a face radiating like the moon. Whoever fasts twenty-nine days of Shaʿbān will attain the greatest satisfaction of Allāh. Whoever fasts thirty days of Shaʿbān will be the recipient of an exclamation from Jibraʾīl at the foot of the Throne as thus: “O’ person, begin anew your deeds, for you have been wholly forgiven for whatever has passed and had been brought forth of your sins!” The Most Glorious—Allāh (azwj)—will then say: “Had your sins been as numerous, even, as the stars in the sky, the raindrops in downpours, the leaves of trees, and the grains of sand, and riches, and the days of the world, you have been forgiven for all of them, and that is not in the least difficult for Allāh after what you have fasted in the month of Shaʿbān!” Ibn ʿAbbās made one last comment: “And this is all for the month of Shaʿbān.”

category: The Book of Merits of Shaʿbān
chapter: The Merits of Shaʿbān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Yaḥya al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him, among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from Nūḥ b. Shuʿayb al-Nīshābūrī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Dahqān, from ʿUrwa b. Abī Shuʿayb al-ʿAqarqūfī, from Shuʿayb, from Abī Baṣīr, who said that he heard al-Ṣādiq (as) narrating from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who transmitted the following report: “One day, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said to his companions: “Which one of you is constantly fasting?” Salmān replied: “I am, o’ Messenger of Allāh.” So the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) then said: “Which one of you stays up all night (in worship)?” Salmān responded: “I do, o’ Messenger of Allāh.” He continued: “Which one of you reads the whole Qurʾān every day?” Again, Salmān was the one to respond: “I do, o’ Messenger of Allāh.” Some of the companions were incensed at that, spurring them to say: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, Salmān is a man from Fars who wants to exult over us, the generality of the Quraysh. You asked us: “Which one of you is constantly fasting?” and he said: “Yes,” even though he often spends his days eating. You asked us: “Which one of you stays up all night (in worship)?” and he said: “Yes,” even though he often spends his nights sleeping. You asked us: “Which one of you reads the whole Qurʾān every day?” and he said: “Yes,” even though he often spends his days silent.” The Holy Prophet (sawa) responded: “Enough, o’ obscure person! And how can you compare to someone like Luqmān the Wise? Ask Salmān, and he will inform you.” The man asked Salmān: “O’ Abā ʿAbd Allāh, do you not claim that you are constantly fasting?” Salmān said: “Aye.” The man continued: “Yet I see you spending many of your days eating.” Salmān defended himself: “It is not as you suppose. I fast three days every month, and Allāh says: ﴾Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times the like thereof﴿ [6:160], and I join fasting in Shaʿbān to the month of Ramaḍān, so that counts as constantly fasting.” The man continued: “And do you not claim that you stay awake at night (to worship)?” Salmān responded: “Aye.” The man retorted: “And yet you spend many of your nights asleep.” Salmān again defended himself: “It is not as you think. I have heard the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) say: “Whoever sleeps in a state of ritual purity, he will have done so as if he had spent the whole night in worship,” and I rest in a state of ritual purity.” The man continued: “Do you not claim that you read the whole Qurʾān every day?” Salmān answered: “Aye.” The man continued: “And yet you spend your days in silence.” Salmān defended himself yet again: “It is not as you think. I have heard my beloved Messenger of Allāh (sawa) say to ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib: “O’ Abāʿl-Ḥasan, the likeness of you in this community is ﴾Say, “He is Allāh, [Who is] One”﴿ [112:1]. Whoever reads that chapter once has read a third of the Qurʾān. Whoever reads that chapter twice has read two thirds of the Qurʾān. Whoever reads that chapter thrice has completed the Qurʾān. Whoever proclaims his love for you with his tongue has completed one third of true belief. Whoever proclaims his love for you with his tongue and his heart has completed two thirds of true belief. Whoever proclaims his love for you with his tongue and his heart and supports you with physical exertion has completed his true belief. O’ ʿAlī, by He Who sent me forth with the Truth, had all the people of the earth loved you as the people of the heavens have done so, no one would be subjected to Hellfire!” And I read (the chapter that begins with) ﴾Say, “He is Allāh, [Who is] One”﴿ thrice every day.” The man stood still as if he had been compelled to swallow a rock.”
arabicText: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن يحيى العطّار، قال: حدثنا أبي، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن نوح بن شعيب النيشابوري، عن عبد الله بن عبد الله الدهقان، عن عروة ابن أخي شعيب العقرقوفي، عن شعيب، عن أبي بصير، قال: سمعت الصادق (عليه السلام) يحدث، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يوماً لأصحابه: أيكم يصوم الدهر؟ فقال سلمان: أنا يا رسول الله، فقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): فأيكم يحيي الليل؟ فقال سلمان: أنا يا رسول الله، قال: فأيكم يختم القرآن في كل يوم؟ فقال سلمان: أنا يا رسول الله، فغضب بعض أصحابه فقال: يا رسول الله، إن سلمان رجل من الفرس يريد أن يفتخر علينا معاشر قريش، قلت: أيكم يصوم الدهر؟ فقال: أنا، وهو أكثر أيامه يأكل، وقلت: أيكم يحيى الليل؟ فقال: أنا، وهو أكثر ليله ينام، وقلت: أيكم يختم القرآن في كل يوم؟ فقال: أنا، وهو أكثر نهاره صامت، فقال النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله): مه يا فلان! أنى لك بمثل لقمان الحكيم سله فإنه ينبئك، فقال الرجل لسلمان: يا أبا عبد الله، أليس زعمت أنك تصوم الدهر؟ قال: نعم، فقال: رأيتك في أكثر نهارك تأكل، فقال: ليس حيث تذهب إني أصوم الثلاثة في الشهر وقال الله: ﴿مَن جَآءَ بِٱلْحَسَنَةِ فَلَهُۥ عَشْرُ أَمْثَالِهَا﴾ وأصل شعبان بشهر رمضان فذلك صوم الدهر، فقال: أليس زعمت أنك تحيي الليل؟ فقال: نعم، فقال: أنت أكثر ليلك نائم فقال: ليس حيث تذهب، ولكني سمعت رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يقول: من نام على طهر فكأنما أحيى الليل كله وأنا أبيت على طهر، فقال: أليس زعمت أنك تختم القرآن في كل يوم؟ قال: نعم، قال: فإنك أيامك صامت، فقال: ليس حيث تذهب، ولكني سمعت حبيبي رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يقول لعلي بن أبي طالب: يا أبا الحسن مثلك في أمتي مثل ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾، فمن قرأها مرة فقد قرأ ثلث القرآن، ومن قرأها مرتين فقد قرأ ثلثي القرآن، ومن قرأها ثلاثاً فقد ختم القرآن، ومن أحبك بلسانه فقد كمل له ثلث الايمان، ومن أحبك بلسانه وقلبه فقد كمل له ثلثاً الايمان، ومن أحبك بلسانه وقلبه ونصرك بيده فقد استكمل الايمان، والذي بعثني بالحق يا علي، لو أحبك أهل الأرض كمحبة أهل السماء لك، لما عذب أحد بالنار، وأنا اقرأ ﴿قُلْ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ أَحَدٌ﴾ في كل يوم ثلاث مرات، فقام وكأنه ألقم حجراً.
