chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad b. Marwān, who said: “I heard al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), saying: “Indeed, for Allāh (taa) there is—on every night of the month of Ramaḍān—(the responsibility of) freeing and releasing people from the Fire, except for those who break their fast on an intoxicant. When the last night occurs, Allāh frees as many people (from Perdition) as He has done throughout the rest of the month.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا الحسين بن الحسن، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن ابن أبي عمير، عن جميل بن صالح، عن محمد بن مروان، قال: سمعت الصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام) يقول: إن لله تعالى في كل ليلة من شهر رمضان عتقاء وطلقاء من النار إلا من أفطر على مسكر فإذا كان آخر ليلة منه أعتق فيها مثل ما أعتقه في جميعه.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Jamīl b. Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad b. Marwān, who said: “I heard al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Indeed, for Allāh (taa) there is—on every night of the month of Ramaḍān—(the responsibility of) freeing and releasing people from the Fire, except for those who break their fast on an intoxicant. When the last night occurs, Allāh frees as many people (from Perdition) as He has done throughout the rest of the month.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Sayf b. ʿUmayra, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh, from the one who heard from Abā Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as), who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said to Bilāl as the month of Ramaḍān approached and three nights yet remained of Shaʿbān: “Call out to the people,” so Bilāl gathered the people. The Holy Prophet (sawa) ascended the pulpit, praised Allāh and extolled Him, then said: “O’ people! This month has approached you, and it is the master of the months. In it is a night better than a thousand months, in which the gates of Perdition are closed and the gates of Paradise are opened. Whoever reaches it and is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him! Whoever knows his parents (and does his duty by them) but is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him! And whoever hears mention of me and does not send blessings upon me yet is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him!”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن سيف بن عميرة، عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله، عمن سمع أبا جعفر الباقر (عليه السلام) يقول: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) لما حضر شهر رمضان وذلك لثلاث بقين من شعبان قال لبلال: ناد في الناس فجمع الناس، ثم صعد المنبر فحمد الله وأثنى عليه، ثم قال: أيها الناس إن هذا الشهر قد حضركم وهو سيد الشهور، فيه ليلة خير من الف شهر، تغلق فيه أبواب النيران، وتفتح فيه أبواب الجنان، فمن أدركه فلم يغفر له فأبعده الله، ومن أدرك والديه فلم يغفر له فأبعده الله، ومن ذكرت عنده فصلى علي فلم يغفر له فأبعده الله.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from Sayf b. ʿUmayra, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh, from the one who heard from Abā Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said to Bilāl as the month of Ramaḍān approached and three nights yet remained of Shaʿbān: “Call out to the people,” so Bilāl gathered the people. The Holy Prophet (sawa) ascended the pulpit, praised Allāh and extolled Him, then said: “O’ people! This month has approached you, and it is the master of the months. In it is a night better than a thousand months, in which the gates of Perdition are closed and the gates of Paradise are opened. Whoever reaches it and is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him! Whoever knows his parents (and does his duty by them) but is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him! And whoever hears mention of me and does not send blessings upon me yet is not forgiven—may Allāh distance him!”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Saʿīd al-ʿAskarī narrated to him, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad al-ʿIjlī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd b. Yaḥyā al-Ḥamānī narrated to him among others, saying that Abū Bakr al-Hadhalī narrated to him among others, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said: “When the month of Ramaḍān would come, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) would free every captive and grant every seeker (of assistance) that which they asked for.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم، قال: حدثني علي بن سعيد العسكري، قال: حدثنا الحسين بن علي بن الأسود العجلي، قال: حدثنا عبد الحميد بن يحيى الحماني، قال: حدثنا أبو بكر الهذلي، عن الزهري، عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله، عن ابن عبّاس، قال: كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) إذا دخل شهر رمضان أطلق كل أسير وأعطى كل سائل.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Saʿīd al-ʿAskarī narrated to him, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. al-Aswad al-ʿIjlī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd b. Yaḥyā al-Ḥamānī narrated to him among others, saying that Abū Bakr al-Hadhalī narrated to him among others, from al-Zuhrī, from ʿUbayd Allāh b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Ibn ʿAbbās, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “When the month of Ramaḍān would come, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) would free every captive and grant every seeker (of assistance) that which they asked for.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Jaʿfar b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mughīra narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl b. Abī Ziyād, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) once said to his companions: “Shall I inform you of something which, if you were to know of it, would drive Shayṭān as far away from you as the East is from the West?” They replied: “Yes!” He continued: “Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for Allāh and supporting one another in righteous deeds cuts off his roots, and seeking forgiveness (from Allāh) severs his lifeline. And for everything, there is an alms-tax, and fasting is the alms-tax of the body.”
arabicText: حدثنا جعفر بن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن عبد الله بن المغيرة، عن إسماعيل بن أبي زياد، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) لأصحابه: ألا أخبركم بشئ إن أنتم فعلتموه تباعد الشيطان عنكم كما تباعد المشرق من المغرب؟ قالوا: بلى، قال: الصوم يسود وجهه والصدقة تكسر ظهره والحب في الله والمؤازرة على العمل الصالح يقطع دابره والاستغفار يقطع وتينه، ولكل شئ زكاة وزكاة الأبدان الصيام.
thaqalaynSanad: Jaʿfar b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Mughīra narrated to us, from Ismāʿīl b. Abī Ziyād, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) once said to his companions:
thaqalaynMatn: “Shall I inform you of something which, if you were to know of it, would drive Shayṭān as far away from you as the East is from the West?” They replied: “Yes!” He continued: “Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for Allāh and supporting one another in righteous deeds cuts off his roots, and seeking forgiveness (from Allāh) severs his lifeline. And for everything, there is an alms-tax, and fasting is the alms-tax of the body.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī Majīlawayh narrated to us, saying that his paternal uncle, Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim, narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from Yūnus b. Ẓibyān, who said: “I said to Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq (as): “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is that which will drive Iblīs away from us?” So he replied: “Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for Allāh and supporting one another in righteous deeds cuts off his roots, and seeking forgiveness (from Allāh) severs his lifeline.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن علي ماجيلويه، قال: حدثنا عمي محمد بن أبي القاسم، عن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله البرقي، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن سنان، عن المفضّل بن عمر، عن يونس بن ظبيان، قال: قلت للصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام): يا ابن رسول الله ما الذي يباعد عنا إبليس؟ قال: الصوم يسود وجهه، والصدقة تكسر ظهره، والحب في الله والمؤازرة على العمل الصالح يقطعان دابره، والاستغفار يقطع وتينه.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī Majīlawayh narrated to us, saying that his paternal uncle, Muḥammad b. Abī’l-Qāsim, narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from Yūnus b. Ẓibyān, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I said to Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq (as): “O’ son of the Messenger of Allāh, what is that which will drive Iblīs away from us?” So he replied: “Fasting blackens his face, charity breaks his back, love for Allāh and supporting one another in righteous deeds cuts off his roots, and seeking forgiveness (from Allāh) severs his lifeline.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Kumaydhānī narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd, from ʿUtba b. Hārūn, saying that Abū Yazīd narrated to him among others, from Ḥaṣīn, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), for Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) has said: “Upon you in the month of Ramaḍān is much seeking of forgiveness and supplication. As for supplication, it draws away affliction from you, and as for seeking forgiveness, it erases your sins.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا علي بن موسى الكميذاني، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن علي بن الحسين، عن محمد بن عبيد، عن عتبة بن هارون، قال: حدثنا أبو يزيد، عن حصين، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام): عليكم في شهر رمضان بكثرة الاستغفار والدعاء، فأما الدعاء فيدفع عنكم به البلاء، فأما الاستغفار فتمحى به ذنوبكم.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Kumaydhānī narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā narrated to him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, from Muḥammad b. ʿUbayd, from ʿUtba b. Hārūn, saying that Abū Yazīd narrated to him among others, from Ḥaṣīn, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), for Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Upon you in the month of Ramaḍān is much seeking of forgiveness and supplication. As for supplication, it draws away affliction from you, and as for seeking forgiveness, it erases your sins.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn b. Mūsā, from Ghiyāth b. Ibrāhīm, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who reported: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Indeed, Allāh (twt) declared six things abhorrent for me, and I declare them abhorrent for the Successors from my progeny and those who follow them after me: purposeless playfulness during prayer, obscenity during fasting, reminding others of one’s charity, entering the mosques in a state of major ritual impurity (from sexual activity), intruding into people’s residences, and laughing in graveyards.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن الصفّار، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن الحسين بن موسى، عن غياث بن إبراهيم، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): إن الله تبارك وتعالى كره لي ست خصال وكرهتهن للأوصياء من ولدي وأتباعهم من بعدي: العبث في الصلاة، والرفث في الصيام والمن بعد الصدقة، وإتيان المساجد جنباً، والتطلع في الدور، والضحك بين القبور.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥusayn b. Mūsā, from Ghiyāth b. Ibrāhīm, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who reported: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Indeed, Allāh (twt) declared six things abhorrent for me, and I declare them abhorrent for the Successors from my progeny and those who follow them after me: purposeless playfulness during prayer, obscenity during fasting, reminding others of one’s charity, entering the mosques in a state of major ritual impurity (from sexual activity), intruding into people’s residences, and laughing in graveyards.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), from his father, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar, from his father, al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, al-Bāqir, from his father, Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn, from his father, the Master of the Martyrs, al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī, from his father, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, the Master of the Successors (as-p), who has said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) delivered a sermon to us one day, in which he said: “O’ people, indeed the month of Allāh has come to you with blessing, mercy, and forgiveness, and it is the most favoured month in the sight of Allāh. Its days are the most favoured days, its nights are the most favoured nights, and its hours the most favoured hours. It is a month in which you are invited to be Allāh’s guests and one in which Allāh has made you the people of honour. Your breaths in the month of Ramaḍān are glorification (of Allāh), your sleeping is worship, your deeds are accepted, and your supplications answered. So ask Allāh, your Lord, with earnest intentions and pure hearts, that He grant you success in fasting for His sake and in recitation of His Book. Indeed, the wretched is he who is debarred from the forgiveness of Allāh in this great month. Remember with your hunger and your thirst during the month of Ramaḍān the hunger and thirst that will ensue on the Day of Reckoning. Be charitable to your paupers and your destitute ones, respect your elders, be merciful to your youngsters, keep relations with your kin, and guard your tongues. Turn the other cheek to that which is impermissible to look at with your eyes or hear with your ears. Have compassion upon the orphans of people so that they may have mercy upon your orphans, and repent to Allāh for your sins. Raise your hands to Him in supplication in the times of your prayers, for it is the best of hours, in which Allāh (azwj) looks upon His servants with mercy, answers them when they invoke Him, responds to them when they call upon Him, and rejoins them when they supplicate to Him. O’ people, your souls are held hostage by your deeds, so pay their ransom by seeking forgiveness, and your backs are weighed down by your burdens, so free them with long prostrations. Know that Allāh—may His remembrance be exalted—has sworn by His grandeur that He will not punish those who pray and prostrate, nor will He terrify them with the Fire on the Day on which men will be made to stand before the Lord of the Worlds. O’ people, he who helps a fasting believer break their fast in this month is, in the eyes of Allāh, like someone who frees a slave and has earned forgiveness for what has already passed of his sins.” It was said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, not all of us are capable of that.” He (as) continued: “Fear the Fire, even if it is by means of a split date. Fear the Fire, even if it is by means of a drink of water. O’ people, he among you who improves his character during this month will have a means of safe passage upon the Bridge on the Day when feet upon the Bridge will shake (having found no firm grounding). Whoever lightens the burden of that which his right hand possesses will have Allāh lighten his accountability. Whoever restrains the evil of his hands in this month, Allāh will restrain the wrath of His hands on the Day he meets Him. Whoever honours an orphan during this month, Allāh will honour him on the day he meets Him. Whoever keeps ties with his kin, Allāh will keep ties between him and His mercy on the Day he meets Him, while whoever cuts ties with his kin, Allāh will cut ties between him and His mercy on the Day he meets Him. Whoever performs voluntary prayers will have absolution from the Fire written for him. Whoever fulfils an obligation in this month will have the reward of seventy obligations fulfilled in any other month. Whoever abundantly sends salutations upon me in this month, Allāh will make the Scale heavy (with good deeds attributed to him) when the Scales will be light (for everyone else). Whoever recites one verse of the Qurʾān in this month will be rewarded with the likeness of completing the entire Qurʾān in any other month. O’ people, the gates of the Paradisiacal realms are opened to you in this month, so ask your Lord not to shut them to you, while the gates of the Fires of Perdition are shut to you, so ask your Lord not to open them to you. And the devils are shackled, so ask your Lord not to let them gain mastery over you.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) reported that he [stood up—according to some manuscripts—and] said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is the best action to do in this month?,” so he replied: “O’ Abā’l-Ḥasan, it is to abstain from that which Allāh has prohibited.” Then he began weeping. I said: “Why are you weeping, o’ Messenger of Allāh?,” so he replied: “O’ ʿAlī, I weep for what will be facilitated against you in this month. It is as if I am with you, as you pray to your Lord, while the most wretched among the first and the last, the brother (in perdition) of he who hamstrung the she-camel of Thamūd, shall strike you on your head between your “horns” with such a strike that stains your beard with blood.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn is reported to have asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, will that happen while I am secure in my religion?,” so the Holy Prophet (sawa) replied: “(Aye, it will happen while) you are secure in your religion.” He (as) continued: “O’ ʿAlī, whoever kills you has killed me, and whoever despises you has despised me, and whoever insults you has insulted me, because you are from me as if you are my own soul, and your spirit is from my spirit, and your clay is from my clay. Indeed, Allāh (twt) has created you and I in particular, chosen you and I in particular, and selected me for prophethood and you for Divine leadership/imāma. So whoever disputes your imāma has disputed me in my prophethood. O’ ʿAlī, you are my successor, the father of my offspring, my daughter's husband, and my caliph presiding over my community in my lifetime and after my death. Your commands are (truly) my commands, and your prohibitions are (truly) my prohibitions. By He Who sent me forth with prophethood and made me the best of creatures, you are the decisive argument of Allāh upon His creation, the safekeeper of His secrets, and His caliph presiding over His servants.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن إسحاق، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد الهمداني، قال: حدثنا علي بن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن أبيه، عن أبي الحسن علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام)، عن أبيه موسى بن جعفر، عن أبيه الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه الباقر، عن أبيه زين العابدين، عن أبيه سيد الشهداء الحسين بن علي، عن أبيه سيد الوصيين أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب (عليهم السلام)، قال: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) خطبنا ذات يوم، فقال: أيها الناس إنه قد أقبل إليكم شهر الله بالبركة والرحمة والمغفرة، شهر هو عند الله أفضل الشهور، وأيامه أفضل الأيام، ولياليه أفضل الليالي، وساعاته أفضل الساعات، هو شهر دعيتم فيه إلى ضيافة الله، وجعلتم فيه من أهل كرامة الله، أنفاسكم فيه تسبيح، ونومكم فيه عبادة، وعملكم فيه مقبول، ودعائكم فيه مستجاب. فاسألوا الله ربكم بنيات صادقة، وقلوب طاهرة، أن يوفقكم لصيامه وتلاوة كتابه، فإن الشقي من حرم من غفران الله في هذا الشهر العظيم، واذكروا بجوعكم وعطشكم فيه جوع يوم القيامة وعطشه، وتصدقوا على فقرائكم ومساكينكم، ووقروا كباركم وارحموا صغاركم، وصلوا أرحامكم واحفظوا ألسنتكم، وغضوا عما لا يحل النظر إليه أبصاركم، وعما لا يحل الاستماع إليه أسماعكم. وتحننوا على أيتام الناس يتحنن على أيتامكم، وتوبوا إلى الله من ذنوبكم، وارفعوا إليه أيديكم بالدعاء في أوقات صلواتكم، فإنها أفضل الساعات ينظر الله عز وجل فيها بالرحمة إلى عباده، يجيبهم إذا ناجوه، ويلبيهم إذا نادوه، ويستجيب لهم إذا دعوه. يا أيها الناس إن أنفسكم مرهونة بأعمالكم، ففكوها باستغفاركم وظهوركم ثقيلة من أوزاركم، فخففوا عنها بطول سجودكم، واعلموا أن الله تعالى ذكره أقسم بعزته أن لا يعذب المصلين والساجدين، ولا يروعهم بالنار يوم يقوم الناس لرب العالمين، أيها الناس من فطر منكم صائماً مؤمناً في هذا الشهر كان له بذلك عند الله عتق نسمة ومغفرة لما مضى من ذنوبه. فقيل: يا رسول الله وليس كلنا يقدر على ذلك فقال (عليه السلام): اتقوا النار ولو بشق تمرة، اتقوا النار ولو بشربة من ماء، أيها الناس من حسن منكم في هذا الشهر خلقه، كان له جوازاً على الصراط يوم تزل فيه الاقدام، ومن خفف في هذا الشهر عما ملكت يمينه خفف الله عنه حسابه ومن كف فيه شره كف الله فيه غضبه يوم يلقاه. ومن أكرم فيه يتيماً أكرمه الله يوم يلقاه، ومن وصل فيه رحمه وصله الله برحمته يوم يلقاه، من قطع رحمه قطع الله عنه رحمته يوم يلقاه ومن تطوع فيه بصلاة كتب له براءة من النار، ومن أدى فيه فرضاً كان له ثواب من أدى سبعين فريضة فيما سواه من الشهور، ومن أكثر فيه من صلاة علي ثقل الله ميزانه يوم تخفف الموازين، ومن تلا فيه آية من القرآن كان له مثل أجر من ختم القرآن في غيره من الشهور. أيها الناس إن أبواب الجنان في هذا الشهر مفتحة فاسألوا ربكم [إن] لا يغلقها عليكم، وأبواب النيران مغلقة فاسألوا ربكم [إن] لا يفتحها عليكم، والشياطين مغلولة فاسألوا ربكم [أن] لا يسلطها عليكم. قال أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) [فقمت خ ل] فقلت: يا رسول الله ما أفضل الأعمال في هذا الشهر؟ فقال: يا أبا الحسن أفضل الأعمال في هذه الشهر الورع عن محارم الله، ثم بكى، فقلت: يا رسول الله ما يبكيك؟ فقال: يا علي أبكي لما يستحل منك في هذا الشهر كأني بك وأنت تصلي لربك وقد أنبعث أشقى الأولين والآخرين شقيق عاقر ناقة ثمود، فضربك ضربة على فرقك [قرنك] فخضب منها لحيتك، قال: أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) فقلت: يا رسول الله ذلك في سلامة من ديني؟ فقال: في سلامة من دينك، ثم قال (عليه السلام): يا علي من قتلك فقد قتلني ومن أبغضك فقد أبغضني، ومن سبك فقد سبني، لأنك مني كنفسي روحك من روحي وطينتك من طينتي، إن الله تبارك وتعالى خلقني وإياك واصطفاني وإياك واختارني للنبوة واختارك للإمامة، ومن أنكر إمامتك فقد أنكرني نبوتي، يا علي أنت وصيي وأبو ولدي وزوج ابنتي، وخليفتي على أمتي في حياتي وبعد موتي، أمرك أمري ونهيك نهي، أقسم بالذي بعثني بالنبوة وجعلني خير البرية إنك لحجة الله على خلقه وأمينه على سره وخليفته على عباده.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), from his father, Mūsā b. Jaʿfar, from his father, al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, al-Bāqir, from his father, Zayn al-ʿĀbidīn, from his father, the Master of the Martyrs, al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī, from his father, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib, the Master of the Successors (as-p), who has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) delivered a sermon to us one day, in which he said: “O’ people, indeed the month of Allāh has come to you with blessing, mercy, and forgiveness, and it is the most favoured month in the sight of Allāh. Its days are the most favoured days, its nights are the most favoured nights, and its hours the most favoured hours. It is a month in which you are invited to be Allāh’s guests and one in which Allāh has made you the people of honour. Your breaths in the month of Ramaḍān are glorification (of Allāh), your sleeping is worship, your deeds are accepted, and your supplications answered. So ask Allāh, your Lord, with earnest intentions and pure hearts, that He grant you success in fasting for His sake and in recitation of His Book. Indeed, the wretched is he who is debarred from the forgiveness of Allāh in this great month. Remember with your hunger and your thirst during the month of Ramaḍān the hunger and thirst that will ensue on the Day of Reckoning. Be charitable to your paupers and your destitute ones, respect your elders, be merciful to your youngsters, keep relations with your kin, and guard your tongues. Turn the other cheek to that which is impermissible to look at with your eyes or hear with your ears. Have compassion upon the orphans of people so that they may have mercy upon your orphans, and repent to Allāh for your sins. Raise your hands to Him in supplication in the times of your prayers, for it is the best of hours, in which Allāh (azwj) looks upon His servants with mercy, answers them when they invoke Him, responds to them when they call upon Him, and rejoins them when they supplicate to Him. O’ people, your souls are held hostage by your deeds, so pay their ransom by seeking forgiveness, and your backs are weighed down by your burdens, so free them with long prostrations. Know that Allāh—may His remembrance be exalted—has sworn by His grandeur that He will not punish those who pray and prostrate, nor will He terrify them with the Fire on the Day on which men will be made to stand before the Lord of the Worlds. O’ people, he who helps a fasting believer break their fast in this month is, in the eyes of Allāh, like someone who frees a slave and has earned forgiveness for what has already passed of his sins.” It was said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, not all of us are capable of that.” He (as) continued: “Fear the Fire, even if it is by means of a split date. Fear the Fire, even if it is by means of a drink of water. O’ people, he among you who improves his character during this month will have a means of safe passage upon the Bridge on the Day when feet upon the Bridge will shake (having found no firm grounding). Whoever lightens the burden of that which his right hand possesses will have Allāh lighten his accountability. Whoever restrains the evil of his hands in this month, Allāh will restrain the wrath of His hands on the Day he meets Him. Whoever honours an orphan during this month, Allāh will honour him on the day he meets Him. Whoever keeps ties with his kin, Allāh will keep ties between him and His mercy on the Day he meets Him, while whoever cuts ties with his kin, Allāh will cut ties between him and His mercy on the Day he meets Him. Whoever performs voluntary prayers will have absolution from the Fire written for him. Whoever fulfils an obligation in this month will have the reward of seventy obligations fulfilled in any other month. Whoever abundantly sends salutations upon me in this month, Allāh will make the Scale heavy (with good deeds attributed to him) when the Scales will be light (for everyone else). Whoever recites one verse of the Qurʾān in this month will be rewarded with the likeness of completing the entire Qurʾān in any other month. O’ people, the gates of the Paradisiacal realms are opened to you in this month, so ask your Lord not to shut them to you, while the gates of the Fires of Perdition are shut to you, so ask your Lord not to open them to you. And the devils are shackled, so ask your Lord not to let them gain mastery over you.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) reported that he [stood up—according to some manuscripts—and] said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is the best action to do in this month?,” so he replied: “O’ Abā’l-Ḥasan, it is to abstain from that which Allāh has prohibited.” Then he began weeping. I said: “Why are you weeping, o’ Messenger of Allāh?,” so he replied: “O’ ʿAlī, I weep for what will be facilitated against you in this month. It is as if I am with you, as you pray to your Lord, while the most wretched among the first and the last, the brother (in perdition) of he who hamstrung the she-camel of Thamūd, shall strike you on your head between your “horns” with such a strike that stains your beard with blood.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn is reported to have asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, will that happen while I am secure in my religion?,” so the Holy Prophet (sawa) replied: “(Aye, it will happen while) you are secure in your religion.” He (as) continued: “O’ ʿAlī, whoever kills you has killed me, and whoever despises you has despised me, and whoever insults you has insulted me, because you are from me as if you are my own soul, and your spirit is from my spirit, and your clay is from my clay. Indeed, Allāh (twt) has created you and I in particular, chosen you and I in particular, and selected me for prophethood and you for Divine leadership/imāma. So whoever disputes your imāma has disputed me in my prophethood. O’ ʿAlī, you are my successor, the father of my offspring, my daughter's husband, and my caliph presiding over my community in my lifetime and after my death. Your commands are (truly) my commands, and your prohibitions are (truly) my prohibitions. By He Who sent me forth with prophethood and made me the best of creatures, you are the decisive argument of Allāh upon His creation, the safekeeper of His secrets, and His caliph presiding over His servants.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan b. Abān narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn b. ʿUlwān, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir (b. Yazīd al-Ju‘fī), from Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as), who said: “When the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) would spy the crescent moon of the month of Ramaḍān, he would turn his face towards the Qibla and then say: “O’ Allāh, let this appear to us with security and faith, peace and Islam, good health and wellness, expansive provision, the repulsion of diseases, recitation of the Qurʾān, and assistance in prayer and fasting. O’ Allāh, secure us for Ramaḍān, secure it for us, and secure it from us until the month of Ramaḍān passes on and You have forgiven us.” Then he would turn his face to the people and state: “O’ throng of Muslims, when the crescent moon heralding the month of Ramaḍān arises, the devils are [or the Devil is] shackled, and the gates of the sky, the gates of the Heavens, and the gates of mercy are opened while the gates to the fires of Hell are shut, and supplications are answered. Every time the fast is broken at sunset, there are people with Allāh (azwj) due for exoneration from the Fire, so He would exonerate them, and then a caller calls out every night: “Is there anyone who wants to ask (Me for something)? Is there anyone seeking forgiveness?” O’ Allāh, give every benefactor a replacement (for what he had freely given others) and give every miser ruination.” When the crescent moon appeared heralding the month of Shawwāl, the believers would be called out: “Proceed to your rewards, for it is the day of reward.” Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) then concluded: “By He in Whose hand is my soul, it is not a reward (counted) in dinars and dirhams.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد، قال: حدثنا الحسين بن الحسن بن أبان، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن الحسين بن علوان، عن عمرو بن شمر، عن جابر، عن أبي جعفر الباقر (عليه السلام)، قال: كان رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) إذا نظر إلى هلال شهر رمضان استقبل القبلة بوجهه ثم قال: « اللهم أهله علينا بالأمن والايمان، والسلامة والاسلام، والعافية المجللة، والرزق الواسع، ودفع الأسقام، وتلاوة القرآن، والعون على الصلاة والصيام. اللهم سلمنا لرمضان وسلمه لنا وسلمه منا حتى ينقضي شهر رمضان وقد غفرت لنا »، ثم يقبل بوجهه على الناس ويقول: يا معشر المسلمين إذا طلع هلال شهر رمضان غلت مردة الشياطين [الشيطان]، وفتحت أبواب السماء وأبواب الجنان وأبواب الرحمة، وغلقت أبواب النيران، واستجب الدعاء، وكان لله عز وجل عند كل فطرة عتقاء يعتقهم من النار ونادى [ينادي خ ل] مناد كل ليلة هل من سائل؟ هل من مستغفر؟ « اللهم اعط كل منفق خلفاً وأعط كل ممسك تلفاً » حتى إذا طلع هلال شوّال نودي المؤمنون أن اغدوا إلى جوائزكم فهو يوم الجائزة، ثم قال أبو جعفر (عليه السلام): أما والذي نفسي بيده ما هي بجائزة الدنانير والدراهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan b. Abān narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from al-Ḥusayn b. ʿUlwān, from ʿAmrū b. Shimr, from Jābir (b. Yazīd al-Ju‘fī), from Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as), who said:

O’ Allāh, secure us for Ramaḍān, secure it for us, and secure it from us until the month of Ramaḍān passes on and You have forgiven us.” Then he would turn his face to the people and state: “O’ throng of Muslims, when the crescent moon heralding the month of Ramaḍān arises, the devils are [or the Devil is] shackled, and the gates of the sky, the gates of the Heavens, and the gates of mercy are opened while the gates to the fires of Hell are shut, and supplications are answered.
