category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī informed him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) that he said: “Verily, for Allāh (twt) are angels acting as agents for the men and women who fast, and they caress these people with their wings, thereby removing their sins from them. Also for Allāh (twt) are angels who have been assigned to seek forgiveness on behalf of fasting men and women, and no one knows the number of these angels except Allāh (azwj).”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن إسحاق، قال: أخبرنا أحمد بن محمد الهمداني، عن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن أبيه، عن أبي الحسن علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام) أنه قال: إن لله تبارك وتعالى ملائكة موكلين بالصائمين والصائمات يمسحونهم بأجنحتهم ويسقطون عنهم ذنوبهم وإن لله تبارك وتعالى ملائكة قد وكلهم بالاستغفار للصائمين والصائمات لا يعلم عددهم الا الله عز وجل.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī informed him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as) that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily, for Allāh (twt) are angels acting as agents for the men and women who fast, and they caress these people with their wings, thereby removing their sins from them. Also for Allāh (twt) are angels who have been assigned to seek forgiveness on behalf of fasting men and women, and no one knows the number of these angels except Allāh (azwj).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) has said to me: “On the last night of the month of Ramaḍān, as many people are given absolution (from Perdition) as in the totality of the rest of the month.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: قال لي أبو جعفر الباقر (عليه السلام): إذا كان آخر ليلة من شهر رمضان أعتق فيها مثل ما أعتق في جميعه.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) has said to me:
thaqalaynMatn: “On the last night of the month of Ramaḍān, as many people are given absolution (from Perdition) as in the totality of the rest of the month.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Saʿdābādī narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from his father, from Khalaf b. Ḥammād al-Ashʿarī, from Abī’l-Ḥusayn al-ʿAbdī, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿIbāya b. Ribʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, who said: “The Holy Prophet (sawa) has said: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall have forgiven whatever preceded him of his sins as well as whatever follows, and whoever stood (to perform supererogatory prayers) in the Night of Power, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall have forgiven whatever preceded him of his sins as well as whatever follows.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن موسى بن المتوكّل، قال: حدثنا علي بن الحسين السعدآبادي، عن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله البرقي، عن أبيه، عن خلف بن حماد الأشهري، عن أبي الحسين العبدي، عن الأعمش، عن عباية بن ربعي، عن عبد الله بن عبّاس، قال: قال النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله): من صام شهر رمضان إيماناً وإحتساباً غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر ومن قام ليلة القدر إيماناً وإحتساباً غفر له ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Saʿdābādī narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī, from his father, from Khalaf b. Ḥammād al-Ashʿarī, from Abī’l-Ḥusayn al-ʿAbdī, from al-Aʿmash, from ʿIbāya b. Ribʿī, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, who said: “The Holy Prophet (sawa) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall have forgiven whatever preceded him of his sins as well as whatever follows, and whoever stood (to perform supererogatory prayers) in the Night of Power, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall have forgiven whatever preceded him of his sins as well as whatever follows.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar (al-Ḥimyarī) narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad (b. ʿĪsā), from Ibn Abī Najrān, who said: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan (al-Riḍā, (as)) saying: “Whoever antagonises our Shīʿa has antagonised us, and whoever befriends our Shīʿa has befriended us. That is because they were created from us, from our clay, and so whoever loves them is from us, and whoever detests them is not. Our Shīʿa perceive with the light of Allāh, and reside in the mercy of Allāh, and triumph through the honours bestowed by Allāh. There is not a single one of our Shīʿa who becomes convalescent except that we become likewise for the sake of his illness, nor one who becomes despondent except that we feel likewise for the sake of his depression, nor one who becomes joyful except that we feel likewise for the sake of his happiness. There is not a single one of our Shīʿa who effectively disappears from our sight, whether they be in the Eastern reaches of the earth, or its West. None of our Shīʿa leave behind a debt to be paid except that its payment is upon us, nor one who leaves behind wealth except that it goes to its rightful inheritors. Our Shīʿa are those who perform the prayer and defray the alms-tax, embark on the pilgrimage to the Sacred House and fast in the month of Ramaḍān. They are partisans of the people of the House (of Muḥammad, (sawa)) and they disavow our enemies—it is these who are the people of belief and piety, active spiritual self-vigilance and righteousness. Whoever stands against them is standing against Allāh, and whoever vilifies them has vilified Allāh, because they are Allāh’s true servants and His sincere allies. By Allāh! Were a single one of them to intercede for as many people as there are in the tribes of Rabīʿa and Muḍar combined, Allāh will accept his intercession, for his honour is upon Allāh (azwj).”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن جعفر، عن أحمد بن محمد، عن ابن أبي نجران، قال: سمعت أبا الحسن (عليه السلام) يقول: من عادى شيعتنا فقد عادانا ومن والاهم فقد والانا لأنهم منا خلقوا من طينتنا من أحبهم فهو منا ومن أبغضهم فليس منا شيعتنا ينظرون بنور الله ويتقلبون في رحمة الله ويفوزون بكرامة الله ما من أحد من شيعتنا يمرض إلا مرضنا لمرضه ولا يغتم إلا اغتممنا لغمه ولا يفرح إلا فرحنا لفرحه ولا يغيب عنا أحد من شيعتنا أين كان في شرق الأرض وغربها. ومن ترك من شيعتنا ديناً فهو علينا ومن ترك منهم مالاً فالورثة شيعتنا الذين يقيمون الصلاة ويؤتون الزكاة ويحجون البيت الحرام ويصومون شهر رمضان ويوالون أهل البيت ويبرؤون من أعدائنا أولئك أهل الإيمان والتقى وأهل الورع والتقوى من رد عليهم فقد رد على الله ومن طعن عليهم فقد طعن على الله لأنهم عباد الله حقاً وأوليائه صدقاً والله إن أحدهم ليشفع في مثل ربيعة ومضر فيشفعه الله فيهم لكرامته على الله عز وجل.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar (al-Ḥimyarī) narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad (b. ʿĪsā), from Ibn Abī Najrān, who said: “I heard Abā’l-Ḥasan (al-Riḍā, (as)) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever antagonises our Shīʿa has antagonised us, and whoever befriends our Shīʿa has befriended us. That is because they were created from us, from our clay, and so whoever loves them is from us, and whoever detests them is not. Our Shīʿa perceive with the light of Allāh, and reside in the mercy of Allāh, and triumph through the honours bestowed by Allāh. There is not a single one of our Shīʿa who becomes convalescent except that we become likewise for the sake of his illness, nor one who becomes despondent except that we feel likewise for the sake of his depression, nor one who becomes joyful except that we feel likewise for the sake of his happiness. There is not a single one of our Shīʿa who effectively disappears from our sight, whether they be in the Eastern reaches of the earth, or its West. None of our Shīʿa leave behind a debt to be paid except that its payment is upon us, nor one who leaves behind wealth except that it goes to its rightful inheritors. Our Shīʿa are those who perform the prayer and defray the alms-tax, embark on the pilgrimage to the Sacred House and fast in the month of Ramaḍān. They are partisans of the people of the House (of Muḥammad, (sawa)) and they disavow our enemies—it is these who are the people of belief and piety, active spiritual self-vigilance and righteousness. Whoever stands against them is standing against Allāh, and whoever vilifies them has vilified Allāh, because they are Allāh’s true servants and His sincere allies. By Allāh! Were a single one of them to intercede for as many people as there are in the tribes of Rabīʿa and Muḍar combined, Allāh will accept his intercession, for his honour is upon Allāh (azwj).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Bakrān al-Naqqāsh narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī, the client of Banī Hāshim, narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl informed him among others, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan, ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), that he said: “Whoever repents of his sins to Allāh (twt) shall have his repentance accepted in the month of Ramaḍān—for it is the month of repentance and absolution, and the month of forgiveness and mercy—and there is not a night from among its nights except that Allāh (twt) frees from the Fire all those due for emancipation who would have been damned to Hell for their sins.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن بكران النقّاش، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد الهمداني مولى بني هاشم، قال: أخبرنا علي بن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن أبيه، عن أبي الحسن علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام) أنه قال: من كان تائباً من ذنب فليتب إلى الله تبارك وتعالى منه في شهر رمضان فإنه شهر التوبة والإنابة وشهر المغفرة والرحمة وما من ليلة من لياليه ولله تبارك وتعالى فيها عتقاء من النار كلهم قد استوجبوا بذنوبهم النار.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Bakrān al-Naqqāsh narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Hamadānī, the client of Banī Hāshim, narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl informed him among others, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan, ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever repents of his sins to Allāh (twt) shall have his repentance accepted in the month of Ramaḍān—for it is the month of repentance and absolution, and the month of forgiveness and mercy—and there is not a night from among its nights except that Allāh (twt) frees from the Fire all those due for emancipation who would have been damned to Hell for their sins.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “It has been said by ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as): “Whoever gives a beggar a loaf of bread in charity at the time when he is supposed to break his fast, Allāh will forgive him his sins and have recorded for him the reward of freeing a slave from among the descendants of Ismāʿīl.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: قال علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام): من تصدق وقت افطاره على مسكين برغيف غفر الله له ذنبه وكتب له ثواب عتق رقبة من ولد إسماعيل.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “It has been said by ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as):
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever gives a beggar a loaf of bread in charity at the time when he is supposed to break his fast, Allāh will forgive him his sins and have recorded for him the reward of freeing a slave from among the descendants of Ismāʿīl.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “It has been said by ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as): “Whoever recites the following supplication at the time of his breaking the fast—O’ Allāh, for You we fasted, through Your success, and with Your sustenance we broke our fast, by Your command. So accept it from us and forgive us, for indeed You are the Forgiving, the innately Merciful—Allāh will forgive him of what he missed out on in his fasting, as well as his sins.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: قال علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام): من قال عند إفطاره: « اللهم لك صمنا بتوفيقك وعلى رزقك أفطرنا بأمرك فتقبله منا واغفر لنا إنك أنت الغفور الرحيم »، غفر الله ما ادخل على صومه من النقصان بذنوبه.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, he—presumably al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl—said: “It has been said by ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as):
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever recites the following supplication at the time of his breaking the fast—O’ Allāh, for You we fasted, through Your success, and with Your sustenance we broke our fast, by Your command. So accept it from us and forgive us, for indeed You are the Forgiving, the innately Merciful—Allāh will forgive him of what he missed out on in his fasting, as well as his sins.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan b. Abān narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ibrāhīm b. Abī’l-Bilād, from his father, who raised it up to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as). When the Imam was asked about a day (in the month of Ramaḍān) which is cast into doubt, he said: “I fast a day of Shaʿbān, liking that I extend it until I break the fast (at the end of) a day of the month of Ramaḍān.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا الحسين بن الحسن بن أبان، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن إبراهيم بن أبي البلاد، عن أبيه، رفعه إلى أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) أنه سئل عن اليوم المشكوك فيه فقال: أصوم يوماً من شعبان أحب إلى من أن أفطر يوماً من شهر رمضان.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. al-Ḥasan b. Abān narrated to him among others, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from Ibrāhīm b. Abī’l-Bilād, from his father, who raised it up to Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as).
thaqalaynMatn: When the Imam was asked about a day (in the month of Ramaḍān) which is cast into doubt, he said: “I fast a day of Shaʿbān, liking that I extend it until I break the fast (at the end of) a day of the month of Ramaḍān.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān b. ʿĪsā, from Samāʿa b. Mihrān, who said: “I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) about the case of a man who fasts on the first day of the month of Ramaḍān while he is in doubt and does not know whether his doing so was of Shaʿbān or of Ramaḍān, even though it is actually the month of Ramaḍān, so he answered: “It is an accepted day, requiring no compensatory act for it.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، عن الحسين بن سعيد، عن عثمان بن عيسى، عن سماعة بن مهران، قال: سألت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) عن رجل صام أول يوم من شهر رمضان وهو شاك لا يدري أمن شعبان أم من رمضان وكان من شهر رمضان فقال: هو يوم وفق لا قضاء له.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn b. Saʿīd, from ʿUthmān b. ʿĪsā, from Samāʿa b. Mihrān, who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “I asked Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) about the case of a man who fasts on the first day of the month of Ramaḍān while he is in doubt and does not know whether his doing so was of Shaʿbān or of Ramaḍān, even though it is actually the month of Ramaḍān, so he answered: “It is an accepted day, requiring no compensatory act for it.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Aḥmad b. Hārūn al-Fāmī (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar b. Jāmiʿ narrated to him, from his father, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from Masʿada al-Ribʿī, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who said that: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) delivered a sermon on the first day of the month of Ramaḍān, in the Great Mosque of Kufa, in which he praised Allāh with the highest praise, honour and eloquence, and commended Him with the most beautiful words of commendation, and then heaped salutations upon His Prophet, Muḥammad (sawa), and then he said: “O’ people! Indeed, the month at present is one which Allāh has favoured over all the other months as He has favoured us, the People of the House, over all other people. It is the month in which the gates of the sky and the gates of mercy are opened up, and the gates of the pits of Hell are shut. It is the month in which exclamations are heard, supplications are answered, and mercy is had upon he who weeps profusely. It is the month in which there is a night wherein angels descend from the sky to bear tidings of peace to the fasting men and fasting women, by the permission of their Lord, until the breaking of dawn. It is the Night of Power, in which my Divine authority was established two thousand years before the creation of Ādam (as). Fasting during its corresponding day is more virtuous than fasting for a thousand months, and the deeds done therein are more virtuous than similar deeds done for a thousand months. O’ people! The suns of the month of Ramaḍān rise upon the fasting men and the fasting women, and its moons shine upon them with mercy. There is neither a night nor a day of this month except that righteousness from Allāh (taa) is showered from the sky upon this community. So whoever triumphs with as much as a pearl’s worth of Allāh’s scattering of blessings will be honoured by Allāh on the day he meets Him, and the honour of Allāh upon a servant is not but that He makes Paradise his abode of dwelling. O’ servants of Allāh, this month of yours is not like other months—its days are the most virtuous days, its nights the most virtuous nights, and its hours the most virtuous hours—and it is the month in which the devils are fettered and incarcerated. It is the month in which Allāh increases provisions and extends terms, and has recorded whoever pays court at His House. This is the month wherein the people of belief are accepted with forgiveness, satisfaction, comfort and pleasure, and the appeasements of the Sovereign Judge. O’ faster! Consider your affairs, for you are in your month, a guest of your Lord, so consider how you will behave by night and by day, and how you keep your limbs from disobeying your Lord. See that you are not asleep in the night or heedless during the day, for in that case, your month will pass while your burdens remain, such that when the fasters’ thirst for Divine reward is quenched, you shall be among the losers, and when they receive their success with honour from their King, you shall be among the deprived, and when they experience bliss in the presence of their Lord, you will be among the expelled. O’ faster! If you are banished from the door to your King, then from which door shall you seek Him? If He forbids you, who then will provide you with your sustenance? If He humiliates you, who then will commend you? And if He abases you, who then will honour you? If He abandons you, who then will support you? If He does not accept you among His servants, then to whom will you take your servitude? If He does not overlook your indiscretion, then to whom shall you turn, seeking forgiveness for your sin? And if He demands His right with you, what will your argument then be? O’ faster! Seek proximity to Allāh through the recitation of His Book throughout your days and nights, for indeed the Book of Allāh is an able intercessor on the Day of Reckoning for those who recited it. Reading its verses will cause their ascendancy through the ranks of Heaven, with glad tidings thereof. O’ faster! You are indeed in a month in which your fasting is a duty, your breathing is a glorification (of Allāh), your sleeping is worship, your obedience (to Allāh) is accepted and your sins are forgiven, your voices are heard, and your whispered invocations are subject to Divine mercy. And I have heard my beloved, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa), saying: “Verily! For Allāh (twt), on every night of the month of Ramaḍān, at the time when fasts are completed, there are prospective detainees of Hellfire who Allāh frees—whose number is known to none but Allāh, included in His knowledge of the unseen—and when it is the last night of the month of Ramaḍān, He frees as many in that one night as He has done so in the rest of the month.” A man from Hamdan stood up and exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your beloved has stated about the month of Ramaḍān!,” so the Imam obliged: “By all means! I have heard my brother, and the son of my paternal uncle, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa), saying: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān while restraining his soul from that which is prohibited will be granted admittance into Paradise.” The man from Hamdan again exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your brother, and the son of your paternal uncle, has stated about the month of Ramaḍān!,” so the Imam said: “By all means! I have heard my confidante, the Messenger of Allāh (sws), saying: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall be admitted into Paradise.” The Hamdanite said: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your confidante has stated about this month!,” so the Imam again obliged him thus: “By all means! I have heard the Liege of the first and the last generations, the Messenger of Allāh (sws), saying: “Whoever fasts in Ramaḍān, and does not break his fast—on any of its evenings—with something that is prohibited, he shall be admitted into Paradise.” The Hamdanite then exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what the Liege of the first and the last generations has stated about this month!,” so the Imam replied: “By all means! I have heard the most virtuous among the Prophets and the Messengers, and the spiritually proximate angels, saying: “Verily, the Liege of the Inheritors shall be murdered in the Liege of all the months.” I asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is the Liege of all the months, and who is the Liege of the Inheritors?,” so he replied: “As for the Liege of all the months, that would be the month of Ramaḍān, and as for the Liege of the Inheritors, that would be you, o’ ʿAlī!,” so I said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh! Will that really occur?,” so he said: “Aye! By my Lord, indeed the most wretched of my community, kindred spirit to he who hamstrung the she-camel of Thamūd, shall be raised up, and then strike you with a strike between your horns until the blood flows from your beard!” The people who heard this took up weeping and wailing, while ʿAlī (as) ended his sermon and descended (from the pulpit).”
arabicText: حدثنا أحمد بن هارون الفامي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثني محمد بن عبد الله بن جعفر بن جامع، عن أبيه، عن هارون بن مسلم، عن مسعدة الربعي، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: خطب أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) في أول يوم من شهر رمضان في مسجد الكوفة فحمد الله بأفضل الحمد وأشرفها وأبلغها وأثنى عليه بأحسن الثناء وصلى على محمد نبيه (صلى الله عليه وآله) ثم قال: أيها الناس إن هذا الشهر شهر فضله الله على سائر الشهور كفضلنا أهل البيت على سائر الناس وهو شهر يفتح فيه أبواب السماء وأبواب الرحمة ويغلق فيه أبواب النيران وهو شهر يسمع فيه النداء ويستجاب فيه الدعاء ويرحم فيه البكاء وهو شهر فيه ليلة نزلت الملائكة فيها من السماء فتسلم على الصائمين والصائمات بإذن ربهم إلى مطلع الفجر وهي ليلة القدر فيها ولايتي قبل أن خلق آدم (عليه السلام) بألفي عام، صيام يومها أفضل من صيام الف شهر والعمل فيها أفضل من العمل في الف شهر، أيها الناس إن شموس شهر رمضان لتطلع على الصائمين والصائمات وإن أقماره ليطلع عليهم بالرحمة. وما من يوم وليلة من الشهر إلا والبر من الله تعالى يتناثر من السماء على هذه الأمة فمن ظفر من نثار الله بدرة كرم على الله يوم يلقاها وما كرم عبد على الله إلا جعل الجنة مثواه عباد الله إن شهركم ليس كالشهور أيامه أفضل الأيام ولياليه أفضل الليالي وساعاته أفضل الساعات هو شهر الشياطين فيه مغلولة محبوسة هو شهر يزيد الله فيه الأرزاق والآجال ويكتب فيه وفد بيته وهو شهر يقبل أهل الإيمان بالمغفرة والرضوان والروح والريحان ومرضات الملك الديان. أيها الصائم تدبر أمرك فإنك في شهرك هذا ضعيف ربك انظر كيف تكون في ليلك ونهارك وكيف تحفظ جوارحك عن معاصي ربك، انظر أن لا تكون بالليل نائماً وبالنهار غافلاً فينقضي شهرك وقد بقي عليك وزرك فتكون عند استيفاء الصائمين أجورهم من الخاسرين وعند فوزهم بكرامة مليكهم من المحرومين وعند سعادتهم بمجاورة ربهم من المطرودين. أيها الصائم إن طردت عن باب مليكك فأي باب تقصد وإن حرمك ربك فمن ذا الذي يرزقك وإن أهانك فمن ذا الذي يكرمك وإن أذلك فمن ذا الذي يعزك وإن خذلك فمن ذا الذي ينصرك وإن لم يقبلك في زمرة عبيده فإلى من ترجع بعبوديتك وإن لم يقلك عثرتك عمن ترجو لغفران ذنوبك وأن طالبك بحقه فماذا يكون حجتك. أيها الصائم تقرب إلى الله بتلاوة كتابه في ليلك ونهارك فإن كتاب الله شافع مشفع يوم القيامة لأهل تلاوته فيعلون درجات الجنة بقرائة آياته، بشر أيها الصائم فإنك في شهر صيامك فيه مفروض ونفسك فيه تسبيح ونومك فيه عبادة وطاعتك فيه مقبولة وذنوبك فيه مغفورة وأصواتك فيه مسموعة ومناجاتك فيه مرحومة ولقد سمعت حبيبي رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يقول: إن لله تبارك وتعالى عند فطر كل ليلة من شهر رمضان عتقاء من النار لا يعلم عددهم إلا الله هو في علم الغيب عنده فإذا كان آخر ليلة منه أعتق فيها مثل ما أعتق في جميعه، فقام إليه رجل من همدان فقال: يا أمير المؤمنين زدنا مما حدثك به حبيبك في شهر رمضان، فقال: نعم، سمعت أخي رسول الله وابن عمي رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يقول: من صام شهر رمضان فحفظ فيه نفسه من المحارم دخل الجنة، قال الهمداني: يا أمير المؤمنين زدنا مما حدثك به أخوك وابن عمك في شهر رمضان، قال: نعم، سمعت خليلي رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) يقول: من صام رمضان إيماناً وإحتساباً دخل الجنة، قال الهمداني: يا أمير المؤمنين زدنا مما حدثك به خليلك في هذا الشهر، فقال: نعم سمعت سيد الأولين والآخرين رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) يقول: من صام رمضان فلم يفطر في شئ من لياليه على حرام دخل الجنة، فقال الهمداني: يا أمير المؤمنين زدنا مما حدثك به سيد الأولين والآخرين في هذا الشهر، فقال: نعم، سمعت أفضل الأنبياء والمرسلين والملائكة المقربين يقول: إن سيد الوصيين يقتل في سيد الشهور، فقلت: يا رسول الله وما سيد الشهور ومن سيد الوصيين؟ قال: أما سيد الشهور فشهر رمضان، وأما سيد الوصيين فأنت يا علي! فقلت: يا رسول الله فإن ذلك لكائن؟ قال: إي وربي أنه ينبعث أشقى أمتي شقيق عاقر ناقة ثمود، ثم يضربك ضربة على فرقك تخضب منها لحيتك، فأخذ الناس بالبكاء والنحيب، فقطع (عليه السلام) خطبته ونزل.
thaqalaynSanad: Aḥmad b. Hārūn al-Fāmī (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar b. Jāmiʿ narrated to him, from his father, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from Masʿada al-Ribʿī, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers (as-p), who
thaqalaynMatn: said that: “Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) delivered a sermon on the first day of the month of Ramaḍān, in the Great Mosque of Kufa, in which he praised Allāh with the highest praise, honour and eloquence, and commended Him with the most beautiful words of commendation, and then heaped salutations upon His Prophet, Muḥammad (sawa), and then he said: “O’ people! Indeed, the month at present is one which Allāh has favoured over all the other months as He has favoured us, the People of the House, over all other people. It is the month in which the gates of the sky and the gates of mercy are opened up, and the gates of the pits of Hell are shut. It is the month in which exclamations are heard, supplications are answered, and mercy is had upon he who weeps profusely. It is the month in which there is a night wherein angels descend from the sky to bear tidings of peace to the fasting men and fasting women, by the permission of their Lord, until the breaking of dawn. It is the Night of Power, in which my Divine authority was established two thousand years before the creation of Ādam (as). Fasting during its corresponding day is more virtuous than fasting for a thousand months, and the deeds done therein are more virtuous than similar deeds done for a thousand months. O’ people! The suns of the month of Ramaḍān rise upon the fasting men and the fasting women, and its moons shine upon them with mercy. There is neither a night nor a day of this month except that righteousness from Allāh (taa) is showered from the sky upon this community. So whoever triumphs with as much as a pearl’s worth of Allāh’s scattering of blessings will be honoured by Allāh on the day he meets Him, and the honour of Allāh upon a servant is not but that He makes Paradise his abode of dwelling. O’ servants of Allāh, this month of yours is not like other months—its days are the most virtuous days, its nights the most virtuous nights, and its hours the most virtuous hours—and it is the month in which the devils are fettered and incarcerated. It is the month in which Allāh increases provisions and extends terms, and has recorded whoever pays court at His House. This is the month wherein the people of belief are accepted with forgiveness, satisfaction, comfort and pleasure, and the appeasements of the Sovereign Judge. O’ faster! Consider your affairs, for you are in your month, a guest of your Lord, so consider how you will behave by night and by day, and how you keep your limbs from disobeying your Lord. See that you are not asleep in the night or heedless during the day, for in that case, your month will pass while your burdens remain, such that when the fasters’ thirst for Divine reward is quenched, you shall be among the losers, and when they receive their success with honour from their King, you shall be among the deprived, and when they experience bliss in the presence of their Lord, you will be among the expelled. O’ faster! If you are banished from the door to your King, then from which door shall you seek Him? If He forbids you, who then will provide you with your sustenance? If He humiliates you, who then will commend you? And if He abases you, who then will honour you? If He abandons you, who then will support you? If He does not accept you among His servants, then to whom will you take your servitude? If He does not overlook your indiscretion, then to whom shall you turn, seeking forgiveness for your sin? And if He demands His right with you, what will your argument then be? O’ faster! Seek proximity to Allāh through the recitation of His Book throughout your days and nights, for indeed the Book of Allāh is an able intercessor on the Day of Reckoning for those who recited it. Reading its verses will cause their ascendancy through the ranks of Heaven, with glad tidings thereof. O’ faster! You are indeed in a month in which your fasting is a duty, your breathing is a glorification (of Allāh), your sleeping is worship, your obedience (to Allāh) is accepted and your sins are forgiven, your voices are heard, and your whispered invocations are subject to Divine mercy. And I have heard my beloved, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa), saying: “Verily! For Allāh (twt), on every night of the month of Ramaḍān, at the time when fasts are completed, there are prospective detainees of Hellfire who Allāh frees—whose number is known to none but Allāh, included in His knowledge of the unseen—and when it is the last night of the month of Ramaḍān, He frees as many in that one night as He has done so in the rest of the month.” A man from Hamdan stood up and exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your beloved has stated about the month of Ramaḍān!,” so the Imam obliged: “By all means! I have heard my brother, and the son of my paternal uncle, the Messenger of Allāh (sawa), saying: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān while restraining his soul from that which is prohibited will be granted admittance into Paradise.” The man from Hamdan again exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your brother, and the son of your paternal uncle, has stated about the month of Ramaḍān!,” so the Imam said: “By all means! I have heard my confidante, the Messenger of Allāh (sws), saying: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, with faith in and having accounted for its reward, shall be admitted into Paradise.” The Hamdanite said: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what your confidante has stated about this month!,” so the Imam again obliged him thus: “By all means! I have heard the Liege of the first and the last generations, the Messenger of Allāh (sws), saying: “Whoever fasts in Ramaḍān, and does not break his fast—on any of its evenings—with something that is prohibited, he shall be admitted into Paradise.” The Hamdanite then exclaimed: “O’ Amīr al-Muʾminīn! Narrate to us more of what the Liege of the first and the last generations has stated about this month!,” so the Imam replied: “By all means! I have heard the most virtuous among the Prophets and the Messengers, and the spiritually proximate angels, saying: “Verily, the Liege of the Inheritors shall be murdered in the Liege of all the months.” I asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is the Liege of all the months, and who is the Liege of the Inheritors?,” so he replied: “As for the Liege of all the months, that would be the month of Ramaḍān, and as for the Liege of the Inheritors, that would be you, o’ ʿAlī!,” so I said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh! Will that really occur?,” so he said: “Aye! By my Lord, indeed the most wretched of my community, kindred spirit to he who hamstrung the she-camel of Thamūd, shall be raised up, and then strike you with a strike between your horns until the blood flows from your beard!” The people who heard this took up weeping and wailing, while ʿAlī (as) ended his sermon and descended (from the pulpit).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿĀmir, saying that his father narrated to him, from al-Riḍā (as), who said: “When it is the Day of Reckoning, the months shall be brought forth to the gathering, fronted by the month of Ramaḍān which is furnished with every beautiful ornament, and it will be situated between the months—on that Day—like the way in which the Moon is situated between the stars. The people of the throng will say to one another: “We would have loved it if we recognised these forms!,” so a caller from Allāh (jj) shall call: “O’ gathering of creatures! These forms are the months whose number with Allāh is twelve months in the Book of Allāh from the day He created the Heavens and the Earth—their liege and the most virtuous one of them is the month of Ramaḍān—My month, the virtue of which has been made manifest so that you may recognise it over the other months and so it will intercede for those who fasted from among My male and female servants, and I shall accept its intercession for them.”
arabicText: حدثنا الحسين بن أحمد بن إدريس، عن أبيه، عن عبد الله بن عامر، قال: حدثني أبي، عن الرضا (عليه السلام) أنه قال: إذا كان يوم القيامة زفت الشهور إلى الحشر يقدمها شهر رمضان عليه من كل زينة حسنة فهو بين الشهور يومئذ كالقمر بين الكواكب فيقول أهل الجمع بعضهم لبعض: وددنا لو عرفنا هذه الصور فينادي مناد من عند الله جل جلاله: يا معشر الخلائق هذه صور الشهور التي عدتها عند الله اثنا عشر شهراً في كتاب الله يوم خلق السماوات والأرض سيدها وأفضلها شهر رمضان أبرزتها لتعرفوا فضل شهري على سائر الشهور وليشفع للصائمين من عبادي وإمائي وأشفعه فيهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, from his father, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿĀmir, saying that his father narrated to him, from al-Riḍā (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “When it is the Day of Reckoning, the months shall be brought forth to the gathering, fronted by the month of Ramaḍān which is furnished with every beautiful ornament, and it will be situated between the months—on that Day—like the way in which the Moon is situated between the stars. The people of the throng will say to one another: “We would have loved it if we recognised these forms!,” so a caller from Allāh (jj) shall call: “O’ gathering of creatures! These forms are the months whose number with Allāh is twelve months in the Book of Allāh from the day He created the Heavens and the Earth—their liege and the most virtuous one of them is the month of Ramaḍān—My month, the virtue of which has been made manifest so that you may recognise it over the other months and so it will intercede for those who fasted from among My male and female servants, and I shall accept its intercession for them.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Mūsā (rh) narrated to me, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī narrated to him, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Hishām b. Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The first of what will be asked of the servant when he is brought before Allāh (azwj) is concerning his obligatory prayers, and about his defraying the alms-tax, and about the obligatory fasts, and the pilgrimage, and about our guardianship—for we are the People of the House—and so if he affirmed our guardianship and died upon it, then his prayers, his fasts, his defrayment of alms-tax, and his pilgrimages will be accepted. And if he had not affirmed our guardianship before Allāh (azwj), then not a single thing of his deeds will be accepted.”
arabicText: حدثني محمد بن موسى رحمه الله، قال: حدثني عبد الله بن جعفر الحميري، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطّاب، عن الحسن بن محبوب، عن هشام بن سالم، عن عمار الساباطي، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) قال: أول ما يسئل عنه العبد إذا وقف بين يدي الله عز وجل الصلوات المفروضات وعن الزكاة وعن الصيام المفروض وعن الحج وعن ولايتنا أهل البيت فإن أقر بولايتنا ثم مات عليها قبلت منه صلاته وصومه وزكاته وحجه فإن لم يقر بولايتنا بين يدي الله عز وجل لم يقبل منه شيئاً من أعماله.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Mūsā (rh) narrated to me, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Jaʿfar al-Ḥimyarī narrated to him, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from al-Ḥasan b. Maḥbūb, from Hishām b. Sālim, from ʿAmmār al-Sābāṭī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The first of what will be asked of the servant when he is brought before Allāh (azwj) is concerning his obligatory prayers, and about his defraying the alms-tax, and about the obligatory fasts, and the pilgrimage, and about our guardianship—for we are the People of the House—and so if he affirmed our guardianship and died upon it, then his prayers, his fasts, his defrayment of alms-tax, and his pilgrimages will be accepted. And if he had not affirmed our guardianship before Allāh (azwj), then not a single thing of his deeds will be accepted.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭalḥa al-Nahdī, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated: “Four supplications are not thrown back but rather they open the gates of the sky and are lifted towards the Throne: the supplication of a parent for his child, and that of an oppressed person against the one who oppressed him, the one who made the lesser pilgrimage (al-ʿumra) until he returns (to his home), and the one who is fasting until he breaks his fast.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن الصفّار، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطّاب، عن علي بن النعمان، عن عبد الله بن طلحة النهدي، عن جعفر بن محمد، عن أبيه، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): أربعة لا ترد لهم دعوة وتفتح لها أبواب السماء وتصير إلى العرش: دعاء الوالد لولده، والمظلوم على من ظلمه، والمعتمر حتى يرجع، والصائم حتى يفطر.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭalḥa al-Nahdī, from Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his father, from his forefathers, from ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p), who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Four supplications are not thrown back but rather they open the gates of the sky and are lifted towards the Throne: the supplication of a parent for his child, and that of an oppressed person against the one who oppressed him, the one who made the lesser pilgrimage (al-ʿumra) until he returns (to his home), and the one who is fasting until he breaks his fast.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. Yaḥyā b. ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī narrated to him among others, from Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from Muḥammad b. Sulaymān al-Daylamī, from his father, who said: “I heard al-Ṣādiq (as) saying: “Winter is the spring of the believer—during it, it lengthens his nights so that he seeks assistance from it in standing for (supererogatory) prayer, and it cuts short his days so that he may seek assistance from it in fasting.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن إدريس، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أحمد بن يحيى بن عمران الأشعري، عن إبراهيم بن إسحاق النهاوندي، عن محمد بن سليمان الديلمي، عن أبيه، قال: سمعت الصادق (عليه السلام) يقول: الشتاء ربيع المؤمن يطول فيه ليله فيستعين به على قيامه ويقصر فيه نهاره فيستعين به على صيامه.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. Yaḥyā b. ʿImrān al-Ashʿarī narrated to him among others, from Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq al-Nahāwandī, from Muḥammad b. Sulaymān al-Daylamī, from his father, who said: “I heard al-Ṣādiq (as) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Winter is the spring of the believer—during it, it lengthens his nights so that he seeks assistance from it in standing for (supererogatory) prayer, and it cuts short his days so that he may seek assistance from it in fasting.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Saʿdābādī narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), who said: “Islam is built on five pillars—upon prayer, the obligatory alms-tax, fasting, the pilgrimage (to the Kaaba in Mecca) and the Divine authority of Amīr al-Muʾminīn and the Imams from among his progeny (saa-p).”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن موسى بن المتوكّل، قال: حدثنا علي بن الحسين السعدآبادي، عن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن سنان، عن المفضّل بن عمر، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد (عليه السلام)، قال: بني الاسلام على خمس دعائم: على الصلاة والزكاة والصوم والحج وولاية أمير المؤمنين والأئمة من ولده صلوات الله عليهم.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Saʿdābādī narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Islam is built on five pillars—upon prayer, the obligatory alms-tax, fasting, the pilgrimage (to the Kaaba in Mecca) and the Divine authority of Amīr al-Muʾminīn and the Imams from among his progeny (saa-p).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Ṣāliḥ b. ʿĪsā al-ʿIjlī narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. ʿAlī narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ṣalt narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Bukayr narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbbād b. ʿAbbād al-Muhallabī narrated to him among others, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from Hilāl b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Yaʿlī b. Zayd b. Jadhʿān, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān b. Hubayra, who narrated: “One day, we were in the company of the Messenger of Allāh (sws), when he said: “I saw wondrous things last night (in my dreams).” Ibn Hubayra narrates: “We said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what did you see? Narrate it to us, may ourselves, our families, and our children be sacrificed for your sake!” The Prophet said: “I saw a man from my community to whom the Angel of Death came so that he may seize the man’s soul—but the man’s kindness to his parents also manifested—so ʿIzrāʾīl was forbidden from doing what he came to do. I saw a man from my community upon whom the punishment of the grave was pressing, but his ablutions (in life) came and forbade the torment from affecting him. I saw a man from my community who had been beleaguered by devils, but his remembrance of Allāh (azwj)—in life—came and saved him from being caught in their grasp. I saw a man from my community who had been encircled by the angels of punishment, but his prayers came and forbade those angels from carrying out that punishment. I saw a man from my community tormented by thirst. Every time he reached a basin, he was prevented from drinking from it, but his fasting in (the month of) Ramaḍān came and quenched his thirst, satisfying him. I saw a man from my community, while the Prophets were sitting in circles—every time he tried to come to a circle, he would be expelled—when his ritual baths to cleanse himself of impurity (in life) came and took him by the hand, seating him by my side. I saw a man from my community surrounded by darkness before him, behind him, to his right and to his left, and beneath him—he was dusted in darkness—but his performing the greater (al-ḥajj) and lesser (al-ʿumra) pilgrimages (in life) came and rescued him from that darkness and entered him into illumination. I saw a man from my community who would speak to the believers, but they would not respond in speech to him, so his maintaining relations with his near of kin (in life) came and exclaimed: “O’ throng of believers! Speak to him, for he maintained relations with his near of kin!,” so the believers responded in speech to him and shook his hand, and he became one with them. I saw a man from my community shielding himself from the heat of Hellfire and its embers with his face and hands, when came to him his giving of charity, thereby providing him with shade for his head and a cover for his face. I saw a man from my community who had been taken by the Zabāniyya—the angels tasked with tormenting sinners in Perdition—from every place, whereupon his enjoining of good and forbidding evil (in life) came and rescued him from between them, and placed him among the angels of mercy. I saw a man from my community who was like a corpse fallen prone, between whom and the mercy of Allāh there was a veil. However, his good manners (in life) came and took him by the hand, and admitted him into the mercy of Allāh. I saw a man from my community standing on the edge of Hell, but the hope he placed in Allāh (azwj) saved him from that. I saw a man from my community being windswept into Hell, but the tears he had shed out of fear of Allāh came and excised him from that. I saw a man from my community upon the Bridge, trembling as like a palm frond trembles in a stormy wind, whereupon his positive thinking about Allāh stabilised his footing and allowed him to cross the Bridge. I saw a man from my community upon the Bridge, swaying on occasion—sometimes crawling, sometimes just holding on—when came his salutations upon me (in life), thereby pulling him up on his feet and allowing him to cross the Bridge. I saw a man from my community who stopped at the gates of Paradise. Every gate he stopped at was shut to him, whereupon his sincere testimony that there is no other deity than Allāh came, thereby opening the gates and admitting him into Heaven.” The compiler of this book—Shaykh al-Ṣadūq (ra)—has said: “I included this narration in this section, for in it is a mention of fasting in the month of Ramaḍān.”
arabicText: حدثنا صالح بن عيسى العجلي، قال: حدثنا محمد بن علي بن علي، قال: حدثنا محمد بن الصلت، قال: حدثنا محمد بن بكير، قال: حدثنا عبّاد بن عبّاد المهلبي، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، عن هلال بن عبد الله، عن يعلي بن زيد بن جذعان، عن سعيد بن المسيّب، عن عبد الرحمن بن هبيرة، قال: كنا عند رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) يوماً، فقال: رأيت البارحة عجائب، قال: فقلنا: يا رسول الله وما رأيت حدثنا فداك أنفسنا وأهلونا وأولادنا؟ فقال: رأيت رجلاً من أمتي قد أتاه ملك الموت لقبض روحه فجائه بره بوالديه فمنعه منه، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي عليه عذاب القبر فجائه وضوئه فمنعه منه، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي قد احتوشته الشياطين فجائه ذكر الله عز وجل فنجاه من بينهم، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي قد احتوشته ملائكة العذاب فجائه صلاته فمنعته منهم، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي يلهث عطشاً كلما ورد حوضاً منع فجائه صيام رمضان فسقاه وأرواه، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي والنبيون حلقاً حلقاً كلما أبى حلقة طرد فجائه اغتساله من الجنابة فأخذه بيده فأجلسه إلى جنبي. ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي من بين يديه ظلمة ومن خلفه ظلمة وعن يمينه ظلمة وعن شماله ظلمة ومن تحته ظلمة مستنقعاً في الظلمة فجائه حجه وعمرته فأخرجاه من الظلمة وأدخلاه النور، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي يكلم المؤمنين فلا يكلمونه فجائه صلته الرحم، قال: يا معشر المؤمنين كلموه فإنه كان واصلاً لرحمه، فكلمه المؤمنون وصافحوه وكان معهم، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي يتقي حر النار وشررها بيده ووجهه فجائته صدقته فكان ظلاً على رأسه وستراً على وجهه، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي قد أخذته الزبانيّة من كل مكان فجائه أمره بالمعروف ونهيه عن المنكر فخلصاه من بينهم فجعلاه مع ملائكة الرحمة، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي جاثياً على ركبتيه بينه وبين رحمة الله حجاب فجائه حسن خلقه فأخذ بيده فأدخله في رحمة الله، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي قائماً على شفير جهنم فجائه رجائه من الله عز وجل فاستنقذه من ذلك، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي قد هوى في النار فجائته دموعه التي بكى من خشية الله فاستخرجه من ذلك، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي على الصراط يرتعد كما ترتعد السعفة في يوم ريح عاصف فجائه حسن ظنه بالله فسكن رعدته ومضى على الصراط، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي على الصراط يرجف أحياناً ويحيد أحياناً ويتعلق أحياناً فجائته صلاته علي فأقامته على قدميه ومضى على الصراط، ورأيت رجلاً من أمتي انتهى إلى أبواب الجنة كلما انتهى إلى باب أغلق فجائته شهادة أن لا إله إلا الله صادقاً فافتتحت الأبواب ودخل الجنة. قال مصنف هذا الكتاب رضي الله عنه: ذكرت هذا الحديث في هذا الموضع لما فيه من ذكر صوم شهر رمضان.

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Abi ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Ziyād, from ʿIṣṣām b. Zayd, from Muḥammad b. al-Munkadir [or al-Mukandir], from Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, who narrated: “Verily, the Messenger of Allāh (sws) ascended the pulpit—on the first step—and said: “Āmīn,” then he climbed the second step and said: “Āmīn.” Then he climbed the third step and said: “Āmīn.” They said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, you said “Āmīn” thrice?!,” so he replied: “Jibraʿīl (Gabriel, (as)) came to me and told me: “Woe betide he who mentions you without pronouncing salutations upon you,” so I replied: “Āmīn.” Then he said: “Woe betide he who comes to know the month of Ramaḍān, yet it passes him by without his earning forgiveness,” so I said: “Āmīn.” Then he said: “Woe betide he who knows both of his parents—or one of them—but does not earn admittance into Paradise through them,” so I said: “Āmīn.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن أبي عبد الله البرقي، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن زياد، عن عصام بن زيد، عن محمد بن المنكدر [المكندر]، عن جابر بن عبد الله الأنصاري، قال: إن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) رقى المنبر، فقال: آمين إلى أن رقى الدرجة الأولى، ثم رقى الثانية فقال: آمين، ثم رقى الدرجة الثالثة فقال: آمين، فقالوا: يا رسول الله قلت: آمين ثلاث مرات؟ فقال: جائني جبرئيل (عليه السلام) فقال: شقي عبد ذكرت عنده فلم يصل عليك، فقلت: آمين، ثم قال: شقي عبد أدرك شهر رمضان فانسلخ عنه ولم يغفر له، فقلت: آمين، ثم قال: شقي عبد أدرك والديه أو أحدهما فلم يدخلا الجنة، فقلت: آمين.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Abi ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Ziyād, from ʿIṣṣām b. Zayd, from Muḥammad b. al-Munkadir [or al-Mukandir], from Jābir b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Anṣārī, who narrated:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily, the Messenger of Allāh (sws) ascended the pulpit—on the first step—and said: “Āmīn,” then he climbed the second step and said: “Āmīn.” Then he climbed the third step and said: “Āmīn.” They said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, you said “Āmīn” thrice?!,” so he replied: “Jibraʿīl (Gabriel, (as)) came to me and told me: “Woe betide he who mentions you without pronouncing salutations upon you,” so I replied: “Āmīn.” Then he said: “Woe betide he who comes to know the month of Ramaḍān, yet it passes him by without his earning forgiveness,” so I said: “Āmīn.” Then he said: “Woe betide he who knows both of his parents—or one of them—but does not earn admittance into Paradise through them,” so I said: “Āmīn.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan, ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), who said: “Whoever fasts for three days right at the end of Shaʿbān, thereby connecting it with (the fasts of) the month of Ramaḍān, Allāh shall have it recorded for him that he fasted for two whole consecutive months. And whoever fasts for a (whole instance of) Ramaḍān, having established faith in and having accounted for its reward, will receive absolution from sins as if it were the day his mother gave birth to him.” The Imam (as) continued: “My father narrated to me, from his grandfather (as-d), that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Whoever comes to know the month of Ramaḍān and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him! And whoever comes to know the Night of Power and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him! And whoever has heard mention of me and sends upon me salutations and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him!” Someone said to him: “How can somebody send salutations upon you, o’ Messenger of Allāh, and yet not be forgiven?,” so he (as) replied: “Such salutations are thrown back in the face of a servant (of Allāh) who sends them upon me but neglects to do the same upon the members of my House. Whoever sends salutations upon both me and my House, then he is forgiven.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن إسحاق، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد الكوفي، عن علي بن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن أبيه، عن أبي الحسن علي بن موسى الرضا (عليه السلام)، قال: من صام ثلاثة أيام من آخر شعبان ووصلها بشهر رمضان كتب الله صوم شهرين متتابعين، ومن صام رمضاناً إيماناً وإحتساباً خرج من الذنوب كيوم ولدته أمه. قال (عليه السلام): حدثني أبي، عن جده (عليهما السلام)، أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) قال: من أدرك شهر رمضان فلم يغفر له فأبعده الله، ومن أدرك ليلة القدر فلم يغفر له فأبعده الله، ومن ذكرت عنده فصلى علي ولم يغفر له فأبعده الله. قيل: يا رسول الله كيف يصلي عليك ولم يغفر له؟ فقال (عليه السلام): إن العبد وإذا صلى علي ولم يصل على آلي لفت تلك الصلاة وضرب بها وجهه، وإذا صلى علي وعلى آلي غفر له.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that Aḥmad b. Muḥammad al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from his father, from Abī’l-Ḥasan, ʿAlī b. Mūsā al-Riḍā (as), who said:

And whoever fasts for a (whole instance of) Ramaḍān, having established faith in and having accounted for its reward, will receive absolution from sins as if it were the day his mother gave birth to him.” The Imam (as) continued: “My father narrated to me, from his grandfather (as-d), that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Whoever comes to know the month of Ramaḍān and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him! And whoever comes to know the Night of Power and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him! And whoever has heard mention of me and sends upon me salutations and yet is not forgiven, then may Allāh distance him!” Someone said to him: “How can somebody send salutations upon you, o’ Messenger of Allāh, and yet not be forgiven?,” so he (as) replied: “Such salutations are thrown back in the face of a servant (of Allāh) who sends them upon me but neglects to do the same upon the members of my House. Whoever sends salutations upon both me and my House, then he is forgiven.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh—from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his forefathers (as-p), who have reported that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said: “Shaʿbān is my month, and the month of Ramaḍān is the month of Allāh (twt)! So whoever fasts a day of my month will have Paradise mandated upon him, and whoever fasts two days of it will be made one of the good friends of the Prophets, the speakers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous on the Day of Reckoning, and whoever fasts three days of it will be with me in my station on the Day of Reckoning. And whoever fasts the whole month (of Shaʿbān) and connects it with the month of Ramaḍān, then that is repentance for every sin committed, whether it be venial or cardinal, and including, even, for blood shed unlawfully.”
arabicText: حدثنا علي بن أحمد بن علي بن عبد الله البرقي، قال: حدثني أبي، عن جده أحمد بن أبي عبد الله، عن أبيه، عن ابن فضّال، عن هارون بن مسلم، عن الصادق جعفر بن محمد، عن آبائه (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): شعبان شهري وشهر رمضان شهر الله تبارك وتعالى فمن صام من شهري يوماً وجبت له الجنة، ومن صام منه يومين كان من رفقاء النبيين والصديقين والشهداء والصالحين يوم القيامة، ومن صام ثلاثة أيام كان معي في درجتي يوم القيامة، ومن صام الشهر كله ووصله بشهر رمضان كان ذلك توبة له من كل ذنب صغيراً وكبيراً ولو من دم حرام.
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh—from his father, from Ibn Faḍḍāl, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from al-Ṣādiq, Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad, from his forefathers (as-p), who have reported that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Shaʿbān is my month, and the month of Ramaḍān is the month of Allāh (twt)! So whoever fasts a day of my month will have Paradise mandated upon him, and whoever fasts two days of it will be made one of the good friends of the Prophets, the speakers of truth, the martyrs, and the righteous on the Day of Reckoning, and whoever fasts three days of it will be with me in my station on the Day of Reckoning. And whoever fasts the whole month (of Shaʿbān) and connects it with the month of Ramaḍān, then that is repentance for every sin committed, whether it be venial or cardinal, and including, even, for blood shed unlawfully.”
