author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Yaḥyā narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Zakariyyā narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from Sulaymān al-Marwazī, from al-Riḍā, ʿAlī b. Mūsā (as), that he said: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, establishing faith in and having accounted for its reward, will have forgiven whatever preceded of his sins and whatever comes after of them. The pen will not run upon the fasting person until he breaks his fast, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his fast. The pen will not run upon the pilgrim until he returns to his home, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his pilgrimage. The pen will not run upon the sleeping person until he wakes up, as long as he does not do anything prohibited in his sleep. The pen will not run upon the youth until he reaches biological maturity. The pen will not run upon he who struggles in the way of Allāh until he turns back to his home, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his struggling. Nor will the pen run upon the maniac until he regains sanity, nor will the pen run upon the convalescent individual until he recovers his health.” Then he (as) said: “Verily, the merchandise of Allāh is affordable, so purchase it before it becomes expensive!”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن إبراهيم بن إسحاق، قال: حدثنا عبد العزيز بن يحيى، قال: حدثنا محمد بن زكريّا، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن أبي عبد الله الكوفي، عن سليمان المروزي، عن الرضا علي بن موسى (عليه السلام) أنه قال: من صام شهر رمضان ايماناً واحتسباً غفرت له ذنوبه ما تقدم من ذنبه وما تأخر، وأن الصائم لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يفطر ما لم يأت بشئ فينقض صومه، وإن الحاج لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يرجع ما لم يأت بشئ يبطل حجه، وإن النائم لا يجري عليه القلم حتى ينتبه ما لم يكن يأت على حرام، وإن الصبي لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يبلغ، وإن المجاهد في سبيل الله لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يعود إلى منزله ما لم يأت بشئ يبطل جهاده، وإن المجنون لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يفيق وإن المريض لا يجري عليه القلم حتى يصح، ثم قال (عليه السلام): وإن سلعة الله رخيصة، فاشتروها قبل أن تغلو.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Ibrāhīm b. Isḥāq narrated to us, saying that ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz b. Yaḥyā narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Zakariyyā narrated to him among others, saying that Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from Sulaymān al-Marwazī, from al-Riḍā, ʿAlī b. Mūsā (as), that he said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasts in the month of Ramaḍān, establishing faith in and having accounted for its reward, will have forgiven whatever preceded of his sins and whatever comes after of them. The pen will not run upon the fasting person until he breaks his fast, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his fast. The pen will not run upon the pilgrim until he returns to his home, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his pilgrimage. The pen will not run upon the sleeping person until he wakes up, as long as he does not do anything prohibited in his sleep. The pen will not run upon the youth until he reaches biological maturity. The pen will not run upon he who struggles in the way of Allāh until he turns back to his home, as long as he does not do anything to invalidate his struggling. Nor will the pen run upon the maniac until he regains sanity, nor will the pen run upon the convalescent individual until he recovers his health.” Then he (as) said: “Verily, the merchandise of Allāh is affordable, so purchase it before it becomes expensive!”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh—from his father, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Barqī, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as)—who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sws) has said: “Verily, between Shaʿbān and Shawwāl there is the month of Ramaḍān, in which the Qurʾān was revealed, and it is the month of Allāh, exalted be His mention. It is the month of blessing, and of forgiveness, and of mercy, and of repentance, and of turning to Allāh, and of reciting the Qurʾān, and of seeking forgiveness, and of fasting, and of supplication, and of worship, and of obedience (to Allāh), and of freedom from the Fire, and of success through attainment of Paradise. Whoever does not earn forgiveness in the month of Ramaḍān will not be forgiven until the next, so which of you can trust that you will make it to the next month of Ramaḍān? Fast its fasting as if you were he who sees that he would never perform fasting in it again! How many of those who fasted a year ago have been buried in their graves this year? Now they have become alone and abandoned in the dust. May Allāh awaken you from the slumber of the heedless, and pardon yourselves and ourselves on the Day of Reckoning!”
arabicText: حدثنا علي بن أحمد بن عبد الله بن أحمد بن أبي عبد الله البرقي، قال: حدثني أبي، عن جده أحمد بن أبي عبد الله، عن أبيه، عن علي بن الحسين البرقي، قال: حدثني أبي، عن جده الحسن بن علي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم): إن بين شعبان وشوّال شهر رمضان الذي أنزل فيه القرآن وهو شهر الله تعالى ذكره، وهو شهر البركة وهو شهر المغفرة وهو شهر الرحمة وهو شهر التوبة وهو شهر الإنابة وهو شهر قراءة القرآن وهو شهر الاستغفار وهو شهر الصيام وهو شهر الدعاء وهو شهر العبادة وهو شهر الطاعة وهو شهر العتق من النار والفوز بالجنة، من لم يغفر له في شهر رمضان لم يغفر له إلى قابل فأيكم متثق [يثق] ببلوغ شهر رمضان قابل، صوموه صيام من يرى أنه لا يصوم بعده أبداً، فكم من صائم له عاماً أول أمسى عامكم هذا في القبر مدفوناً؟ وأصبح في التراب وحيداً فريداً ينبهكم الله من رقدة الغافلين وغفر لنا ولكم يوم الدين!
thaqalaynSanad: ʿAlī b. Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Barqī narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—Aḥmad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh—from his father, from ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn al-Barqī, saying that his father narrated to him, from his grandfather—al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as)—who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sws) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily, between Shaʿbān and Shawwāl there is the month of Ramaḍān, in which the Qurʾān was revealed, and it is the month of Allāh, exalted be His mention. It is the month of blessing, and of forgiveness, and of mercy, and of repentance, and of turning to Allāh, and of reciting the Qurʾān, and of seeking forgiveness, and of fasting, and of supplication, and of worship, and of obedience (to Allāh), and of freedom from the Fire, and of success through attainment of Paradise. Whoever does not earn forgiveness in the month of Ramaḍān will not be forgiven until the next, so which of you can trust that you will make it to the next month of Ramaḍān? Fast its fasting as if you were he who sees that he would never perform fasting in it again! How many of those who fasted a year ago have been buried in their graves this year? Now they have become alone and abandoned in the dust. May Allāh awaken you from the slumber of the heedless, and pardon yourselves and ourselves on the Day of Reckoning!”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from Sahl b. Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAbbās b. Juraysh al-Rāzī, from Abī Jaʿfar (al-Thānī)—Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Mūsā b. Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p)—from his father, from his grandfather (as-p)—i.e., Abū Ibrāhīm al-Kāẓim—who reported that al-Ṣādiq (as) said: “I heard my father saying: “There is not a servant (of Allah) who has read the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ a thousand times on Monday and a thousand times on Thursday except that Allāh (twt) has created—because of this recitation—an angel called “al-ʿAwī,” whose reach is greater than the seven skies and seven earths. Upon the place of every atom of his body are a thousand hairs, and in each hair a thousand tongues. Every tongue speaks with the vigour of the tongues of the two heavyweights—humans and jinn—thereby seeking forgiveness for the one who recited the chapter, and the Lord (taa) forgives for two thousand years, a thousand times over.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن موسى بن المتوكّل رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أبي عبد الله الكوفي، عن سهل بن زياد، عن الحسن بن عبّاس بن جريش الرازي، عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي بن موسى بن جعفر بن محمد بن علي بن الحسين بن علي بن أبي طالب (عليهم السلام)، عن أبيه، عن جده (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال الصادق (عليه السلام): سمعت أبي (عليه السلام) يقول: ما قرأ عبد إنا أنزلناه الف مرة يوم الاثنين وألف مرة يوم الخمسين الا خلق الله تبارك وتعالى منها ملكاً يدعى العوي راحته أكبر من سبع سماوات وسبع أرضين، في موضع كل ذرة من جسده الف شعرة، في كل شعرة الف لسان ينطق كل لسان لقوة ألسنة الثقلين يستغفر لقاريها، ويضاعف الرب تعالى استغفار ألفي سنة الف مرة.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Mūsā b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Abī ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, from Sahl b. Ziyād, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAbbās b. Juraysh al-Rāzī, from Abī Jaʿfar (al-Thānī)—Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. Mūsā b. Jaʿfar b. Muḥammad b. ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn b. ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as-p)—from his father, from his grandfather (as-p)—i.e., Abū Ibrāhīm al-Kāẓim—who reported that al-Ṣādiq (as) said: “I heard my father saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “There is not a servant (of Allah) who has read the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ a thousand times on Monday and a thousand times on Thursday except that Allāh (twt) has created—because of this recitation—an angel called “al-ʿAwī,” whose reach is greater than the seven skies and seven earths. Upon the place of every atom of his body are a thousand hairs, and in each hair a thousand tongues. Every tongue speaks with the vigour of the tongues of the two heavyweights—humans and jinn—thereby seeking forgiveness for the one who recited the chapter, and the Lord (taa) forgives for two thousand years, a thousand times over.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, it is reported that Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) said: “Whoever revives the Night of Power shall have his sins forgiven, even if their number were like the stars in the sky, the mass of the mountains, and the depths of the seas.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: قال أبو جعفر الباقر (عليه السلام): من أحيي ليلة القدر غفرت له ذنوبه ولو كانت عدد نجوم السماء ومثاقيل الجبال ومكاييل البحار.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, it is reported that Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as) said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever revives the Night of Power shall have his sins forgiven, even if their number were like the stars in the sky, the mass of the mountains, and the depths of the seas.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: And with the same chain of transmission, it has been narrated that Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as-d) has said: “Whoever recites the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ in the sanctum of Allāh (azwj) a thousand times, Allāh (azwj) will have it recorded for him the reward of every greater (ḥajj) and lesser (ʿumra) pilgrimage that has ever taken place or will ever take place. And whoever recites it at the location of ʿArafa a hundred times will have the reward of those who have struggled in the way of Allāh until the Day of Judgement. And whoever recites it seventy times inside the mosque of Minā will have the reward of every instance of charity given or that will be given until the Day of Judgement. Whoever recites it inside the cavity of the Kaaba will have the rewards of the truthful ones and martyrs until the Day of Judgement. And whoever recites it in the mosque of Medina at the location of the Messenger of Allāh’s (sws) grave twenty-one times will have the reward of all the people of Heaven until the Day of Judgement, and in addition, a reward like that of the Prophets shall be recorded for him.”
arabicText: وبهذا الإسناد، قال: قال أبو جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر (عليهما السلام): من قرأ إنا أنزلناه في حرم الله عز وجل الف مرة كتب الله عز وجل له أجر كل حجة أو عمرة كانت أو تكون، ومن قرأها في موقف عرفة مائة مرة كان له أجر المجاهدين إلى يوم القيامة، ومن قرأها في مسجد منى سبعين مرة كان له أجر كل صدقة تصدق بها أو يتصدق بها إلى يوم القيامة، ومن قرأها في جوف الكعبة كان له أجور الصديقين والشهداء إلى يوم القيامة، ومن قرأها في مسجد المدينة عند قبر رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) إحدى وعشرين مرة كان له أجور أهل الجنة إلى يوم القيامة، وكتب له مثل أجر النبيين.
thaqalaynSanad: And with the same chain of transmission, it has been narrated that Abū Jaʿfar al-Bāqir (as-d) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever recites the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ in the sanctum of Allāh (azwj) a thousand times, Allāh (azwj) will have it recorded for him the reward of every greater (ḥajj) and lesser (ʿumra) pilgrimage that has ever taken place or will ever take place. And whoever recites it at the location of ʿArafa a hundred times will have the reward of those who have struggled in the way of Allāh until the Day of Judgement. And whoever recites it seventy times inside the mosque of Minā will have the reward of every instance of charity given or that will be given until the Day of Judgement. Whoever recites it inside the cavity of the Kaaba will have the rewards of the truthful ones and martyrs until the Day of Judgement. And whoever recites it in the mosque of Medina at the location of the Messenger of Allāh’s (sws) grave twenty-one times will have the reward of all the people of Heaven until the Day of Judgement, and in addition, a reward like that of the Prophets shall be recorded for him.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Mihrān, from Ṣāliḥ b. ʿUqba, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, who said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣādiq (as) mentioned the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ and then said: “Is there anything (more) to clarify about its superiority in virtue over other chapters?” Al-Mufaḍḍal reports: “I said: “And what is that thing due to which it is superior in virtue?” So he replied: “The guardianship of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) was revealed in it.” I retorted: “In the Night of Power which we anticipate in (the month of) Ramaḍān?” He continued: “It is the night in which the heavens and the earth were determined.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، عن محمد بن الحسين بن أبي الخطّاب، عن محمد بن عبد الله بن مهران، عن صالح بن عقبة، عن المفضّل بن عمر، قال: ذكر أبو عبد الله الصادق (عليه السلام) إنا أنزلناه فقال: من أبين فضلها على السور، قال: قلت: وأي شئ أفضلها، قال: نزلت ولاية أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام) فيها، قلت: في ليلة القدر التي نرتجيها من رمضان، قال: هي ليلة قدرت السماوات والأرض فيها.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. al-Ḥusayn b. Abī’l-Khaṭṭāb, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Mihrān, from Ṣāliḥ b. ʿUqba, from al-Mufaḍḍal b. ʿUmar, who said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh al-Ṣādiq (as) mentioned the chapter of ﴾Indeed, We sent it down﴿ and then said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Is there anything (more) to clarify about its superiority in virtue over other chapters?” Al-Mufaḍḍal reports: “I said: “And what is that thing due to which it is superior in virtue?” So he replied: “The guardianship of Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) was revealed in it.” I retorted: “In the Night of Power which we anticipate in (the month of) Ramaḍān?” He continued: “It is the night in which the heavens and the earth were determined.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, from Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Zurāra b. Aʿyan, from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad (al-Bāqir, (as)), who said: “Islam is built on five things—upon prayer, the obligatory alms-tax, fasting, the pilgrimage (to the Kaaba in Mecca), and Divine authority, and the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Fasting is a shield against the Fire.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، عن سعد بن عبد الله، عن يعقوب بن يزيد، عن حماد بن عيسى، عن حريز بن عبد الله، عن زرارة بن أعين، عن أبي جعفر محمد (عليه السلام)، قال: بني الإسلام على خمسة أشياء: على الصلاة والزكاة والصوم والحج والولاية، وقال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): الصوم جنة من النار.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, from Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd, from Ḥammād b. ʿĪsā, from Ḥarīz b. ʿAbd Allāh, from Zurāra b. Aʿyan, from Abī Jaʿfar Muḥammad (al-Bāqir, (as)), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Islam is built on five things—upon prayer, the obligatory alms-tax, fasting, the pilgrimage (to the Kaaba in Mecca), and Divine authority, and the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Fasting is a shield against the Fire.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him among others, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Salmān al-Urmunī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Were the fasting person to see a group of people eating food, or a single man doing so, the fasting person’s hairs—each and every one of them—would engage in glorification (of Allāh).”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا علي بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن السلمان الأرمني، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: إذا رأى الصائم قوماً يأكلون أو رجلاً يأكل سبحت كل شعرة منه.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him among others, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from al-Salmān al-Urmunī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Were the fasting person to see a group of people eating food, or a single man doing so, the fasting person’s hairs—each and every one of them—would engage in glorification (of Allāh).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, from Sahl b. Ziyād al-Ādamī, from Bakr b. Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from ʿUmar b. Yazīd, from Yūnus b. Ẓibyān, who reported that Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) has said: “Whoever fasted for the sake of Allāh (azwj) for a day in severe heat that afflicts him with thirst, Allāh shall appoint a thousand angels to caress his face and give him glad tidings until he breaks his fast, which is when Allāh (azwj) will say: “How naturally sublime is your scent and your spirit! O’ My angels, bear witness that I have forgiven him!”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن يحيى العطّار، عن سهل بن زياد الآدمي، عن بكر بن صالح، عن محمد بن سنان، عن عمر بن يزيد، عن يونس بن ظبيان، قال: قال أبو عبد الله (عليه السلام): من صام لله عز وجل يوماً في شدة الحر فأصابه ظمأ وكل الله به الف ملك يمسحون بوجهه ويبشرونه حتى إذا أفطر قال الله عز وجل: ما أطيب ريحك وروحك، ملائكتي اشهدوا أني قد غفرت له.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, from Sahl b. Ziyād al-Ādamī, from Bakr b. Ṣāliḥ, from Muḥammad b. Sinān, from ʿUmar b. Yazīd, from Yūnus b. Ẓibyān, who reported that Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever fasted for the sake of Allāh (azwj) for a day in severe heat that afflicts him with thirst, Allāh shall appoint a thousand angels to caress his face and give him glad tidings until he breaks his fast, which is when Allāh (azwj) will say: “How naturally sublime is your scent and your spirit! O’ My angels, bear witness that I have forgiven him!”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him among others, from his father—Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim—from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Salama Bayāʿ al-Sābirī, from Abī’l-Ṣabāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “The fasting person enjoys two joys—one occurs at the time of his breaking his fast, and one at the time he meets his Lord (azwj).”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا علي بن إبراهيم، عن أبيه إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن سلمة بياع السابري، عن أبي الصباح الكناني، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) قال: للصائم فرحتان فرحة عند إفطاره وفرحة عند لقاء ربه عز وجل.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm narrated to him among others, from his father—Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim—from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Salama Bayāʿ al-Sābirī, from Abī’l-Ṣabāḥ al-Kinānī, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The fasting person enjoys two joys—one occurs at the time of his breaking his fast, and one at the time he meets his Lord (azwj).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, saying that my father narrated to him among others, from Sahl b. Ziyād al-Azdī, from Manṣūr b. al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAmrū b. Saʿīd, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣadaqa, who reported that Abū’l-Ḥasan (as) has said: “Take a midday nap, for Allāh feeds and quenches the thirst of the fasting person while he is in his sleep.”
arabicText: حدثنا أحمد بن محمد بن يحيى العطّار، قال: حدثنا أبي، عن سهل بن زياد الأزدي، عن منصور بن العبّاس، عن عمرو بن سعيد، عن الحسن بن صدقة، قال: قال أبو الحسن (عليه السلام): قيلوا فإن الله يطعم الصائم في منامه ويسقيه.
thaqalaynSanad: Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to us, saying that my father narrated to him among others, from Sahl b. Ziyād al-Azdī, from Manṣūr b. al-ʿAbbās, from ʿAmrū b. Saʿīd, from al-Ḥasan b. Ṣadaqa, who reported that Abū’l-Ḥasan (as) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Take a midday nap, for Allāh feeds and quenches the thirst of the fasting person while he is in his sleep.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Allāh (twt) revealed to Mūsā (as) the following: “What forbids you from engaging in quiet invocations of Me?” So Mūsā replied: “O’ Lord! I revere You too highly to engage in quiet invocation, considering the odour emanating from the fasting person’s mouth.” So, Allāh (twt) revealed to him: “O’ Mūsā! The odour that emanates from the fasting person’s mouth is more naturally in accordance with My liking than the scent of musk!”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن بن أحمد بن الوليد رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن الحسن الصفّار، عن إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن بعض أصحابنا، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: أوحى الله تبارك وتعالى إلى موسى (عليه السلام): ما يمنعك من مناجاتي؟ فقال: يا رب أجلك عن المناجاة لخلوف فم الصائم، فأوحى الله تبارك وتعالى إليه: يا موسى لخلوف فم الصائم أطيب عندي من ريح المسك.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan b. Aḥmad b. al-Walīd (ra) narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. al-Ḥasan al-Ṣaffār narrated to him among others, from Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from some of our companions, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Allāh (twt) revealed to Mūsā (as) the following: “What forbids you from engaging in quiet invocations of Me?” So Mūsā replied: “O’ Lord! I revere You too highly to engage in quiet invocation, considering the odour emanating from the fasting person’s mouth.” So, Allāh (twt) revealed to him: “O’ Mūsā! The odour that emanates from the fasting person’s mouth is more naturally in accordance with My liking than the scent of musk!”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from Masʿada, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Indeed, Allāh (azwj) has appointed angels as trustees over the supplications of those who fast.” The Prophet has also said: “Jibraʿīl (as) has informed me that my Lord (twt) has said: “I have not commanded my angels (as trustees) upon the supplication of anyone of My creations but that such a person will receive an answer (due to the angels’ trusteeship).”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن هارون بن مسلم، عن مسعدة، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) أن رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله)، قال: إن الله عز وجل وكل ملائكة بالدعاء للصائمين، وقال: أخبرني جبرئيل (عليه السلام) عن ربى تبارك وتعالى أنه قال: ما أمرت ملائكتي بالدعاء لأحد من خلقي إلا استجبت لهم فيه.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from Hārūn b. Muslim, from Masʿada, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Indeed, Allāh (azwj) has appointed angels as trustees over the supplications of those who fast.” The Prophet has also said: “Jibraʿīl (as) has informed me that my Lord (twt) has said: “I have not commanded my angels (as trustees) upon the supplication of anyone of My creations but that such a person will receive an answer (due to the angels’ trusteeship).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Ḥasan, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, from ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭalḥa, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who has stated: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “The fasting person is engaged in worship even if he is sleeping on his mattress, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim.”
arabicText: حدثنا الحسين بن أحمد بن إدريس، قال: حدثنا أبي، عن محمد بن حسان، عن محمد بن علي، عن علي بن النعمان، عن عبد الله بن طلحة، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): الصائم في عبادة وإن كان نائماً على فراشه ما لم يغتب مسلماً.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. Ḥasan, from Muḥammad b. ʿAlī, from ʿAlī b. al-Nuʿmān, from ʿAbd Allāh b. Ṭalḥa, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who has stated: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The fasting person is engaged in worship even if he is sleeping on his mattress, so long as he does not backbite a Muslim.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Salīm, from whoever he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), concerning the saying of Allāh (azwj): ﴾And seek help through patience and prayer﴿ [2:45]: “It means fasting and prayer.” He (as) has also said: “Were a calamity or distress to afflict a man, he ought to fast, for Allāh (azwj) says: ﴾And seek help through patience﴿, which is a reference to fasting.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي، قال: حدثنا علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن أبيه، عن محمد بن أبي عمير، عن سليم، عمن ذكره، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام) في قول الله عز وجل: ﴿وَٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ وَٱلصَّلَوٰةِ﴾ يعني الصيام والصلاة، وقال (عليه السلام): إذا نزلت الرجل النازلة أو الشدة فليصم، فإن الله عز وجل يقول: ﴿وَٱسْتَعِينُوا۟ بِٱلصَّبْرِ﴾ يعني الصيام.
thaqalaynSanad: My father narrated to us, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from his father, from Muḥammad b. Abī ʿUmayr, from Salīm, from whoever he mentioned, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), concerning the saying of Allāh (azwj): ﴾And seek help through patience and prayer﴿ [2:45]:
thaqalaynMatn: “It means fasting and prayer.” He (as) has also said: “Were a calamity or distress to afflict a man, he ought to fast, for Allāh (azwj) says: ﴾And seek help through patience﴿, which is a reference to fasting.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī (b.) Mājīlawayh narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said to me: “May I inform you—without doubt—of the pillar of Islam and its part, its peak and its pinnacle?,” so I replied: “Yes,” so he continued: “Its pillar is prayer and its part is the alms-tax, and its peak and pinnacle are struggle in the way of Allāh. May I inform you of the gates to that which is good? Fasting is a shield (from the Fire).”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن علي ماجيلويه، قال: حدثنا محمد بن يحيى العطّار، عن أحمد بن محمد بن عيسى، عن الحسن بن علي بن فضّال، عن علي بن عبد العزيز، قال: قال لي أبو عبد الله (عليه السلام): ألا أخبرك بأصل الإسلام وفرعه وذروة الإسلام وسنامه، قلت: بلى، قال: أصله الصلاة وفرعه الزكاة وذروته وسنامه الجهاد في سبيل الله ألا أخبرك بأبواب الخير؟ الصوم جنة.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. ʿAlī (b.) Mājīlawayh narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. Yaḥyā al-ʿAṭṭār narrated to him among others, from Aḥmad b. Muḥammad b. ʿĪsā, from al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī b. Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz, who said: “Abū ʿAbd Allāh (as) said to me:
thaqalaynMatn: “May I inform you—without doubt—of the pillar of Islam and its part, its peak and its pinnacle?,” so I replied: “Yes,” so he continued: “Its pillar is prayer and its part is the alms-tax, and its peak and pinnacle are struggle in the way of Allāh. May I inform you of the gates to that which is good? Fasting is a shield (from the Fire).”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to me, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn b. Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as-p), who said that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated: “For everything there is an alms-tax, and the alms-tax of the body is fasting.”
arabicText: حدثني أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا علي بن إبراهيم بن هاشم، عن أبيه، عن الحسين بن يزيد، عن ابن أبي عمير، عن هشام بن الحكم، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، عن آبائه عن أمير المؤمنين (عليهم السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): لكل شئ زكاة وزكاة الأبدان الصيام.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to me, saying that ʿAlī b. Ibrāhīm b. Hāshim narrated to him among others, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn b. Yazīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), from his forefathers, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as-p), who said that the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has stated:
thaqalaynMatn: “For everything there is an alms-tax, and the alms-tax of the body is fasting.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to him among others, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said: “Whoever does not earn forgiveness in the (incumbent) month of Ramaḍān will not earn forgiveness until the next, unless he witnesses ʿArafa.” [1]
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رحمه الله، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، قال: حدثنا يعقوب بن يزيد، عن ابن أبي عمير، عن هشام بن الحكم، عن أبي عبد الله (عليه السلام)، قال: من لم يغفر له في شهر رمضان لم يغفر له إلى قابل الا أن يشهد عرفة.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (rh) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Yaʿqūb b. Yazīd narrated to him among others, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām b. al-Ḥakam, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh (as), who said:
thaqalaynMatn: “Whoever does not earn forgiveness in the (incumbent) month of Ramaḍān will not earn forgiveness until the next, unless he witnesses ʿArafa.” [1]

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq b. ʿAmmār, from al-Masʿamī, that he heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) enjoining his children thus: “When the month of Ramaḍān comes upon you, strive with your own selves, for it is the month in which sustenances are distributed and lifespans are recorded, and those who visit Allāh have their visitation also recorded, and during this month is a night wherein deeds done are better than those done in a thousand months.”
arabicText: حدثنا الحسين بن أحمد بن إدريس، قال: حدثنا أبي، عن محمد بن عبد الجبّار، عن صفوان بن يحيى، عن إسحاق بن عمار، عن المسمعي أنه سمع أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) يوصي ولده ويقول: إذا دخل شهر رمضان فاجهدوا أنفسكم فيه فإن فيه تقسيم الأرزاق ويثبت الآجال ويكتب وفد الله الذين يفدون إليه، وفيه ليلة العمل فيها خير من العمل في الف شهر.
thaqalaynSanad: Al-Ḥusayn b. Aḥmad b. Idrīs narrated to us, saying that his father narrated to him among others, from Muḥammad b. ʿAbd al-Jabbār, from Ṣafwān b. Yaḥyā, from Isḥāq b. ʿAmmār, from al-Masʿamī, that he heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) enjoining his children thus:
thaqalaynMatn: “When the month of Ramaḍān comes upon you, strive with your own selves, for it is the month in which sustenances are distributed and lifespans are recorded, and those who visit Allāh have their visitation also recorded, and during this month is a night wherein deeds done are better than those done in a thousand months.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Shaybānī narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Barmakī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Sinān narrated to him among others, from Ziyād b. al-Mundhir, from Abī Jaʿfar, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Bāqir (as), who has said: “The month of Ramaḍān is the month of Ramaḍān, wherein those who fast are feted by Allāh and are the people of His honour. Whoever has the month of Ramaḍān come to pass upon him and spends its days fasting and engages in prayer for part of its nights, and restrains himself from that which Allāh has prohibited to him, shall be admitted into Paradise without accountability.”
arabicText: حدثنا محمد بن أحمد الشيباني، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أبي عبد الله الكوفي، قال: حدثنا البرمكي، قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن أحمد، قال: حدثنا محمد بن سنان، عن زياد بن المنذر، عن أبي جعفر محمد بن علي الباقر (عليه السلام)، قال: شهر رمضان شهر رمضان والصائمون فيه أضياف الله وأهل كرامته من دخل عليه شهر رمضان، فصام نهاره وقام ورداً من ليله واجتنب ما حرم الله عليه دخل الجنة بغير حساب.
thaqalaynSanad: Muḥammad b. Aḥmad al-Shaybānī narrated to us, saying that Muḥammad b. ʿAbd Allāh al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Barmakī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Sinān narrated to him among others, from Ziyād b. al-Mundhir, from Abī Jaʿfar, Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Bāqir (as), who has said:
thaqalaynMatn: “The month of Ramaḍān is the month of Ramaḍān, wherein those who fast are feted by Allāh and are the people of His honour. Whoever has the month of Ramaḍān come to pass upon him and spends its days fasting and engages in prayer for part of its nights, and restrains himself from that which Allāh has prohibited to him, shall be admitted into Paradise without accountability.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad al-Iṣfahānī, from Sulaymān b. Dāwūd al-Munqarī, from Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth al-Nakhʿī, who narrates: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying: “Verily, fasting in the month of Ramaḍān has not been ordained by Allāh upon any of the communities before us.” I retorted: “And what of Allāh’s (azwj) saying: ﴾O’ believers! Fasting has been prescribed for you—as it was for those before you—so perhaps you will become mindful of Allāh﴿?” [2:183], so he replied: “Allāh ordained fasting in the month of Ramaḍān only upon the Prophets, and not their respective communities as well. Thus, Allāh has favoured this community with it and made fasting a duty upon the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) and his community.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبي رضي الله عنه، قال: حدثنا سعد بن عبد الله، عن القاسم بن محمد الإصفهاني، عن سليمان بن داود المنقري، عن حفص بن غياث النخعي، قال: سمعت أبا عبد الله (عليه السلام) يقول: إن شهر رمضان لم يفرض الله صيامه على أحد من الأمم قبلنا، فقلت له: فقول الله عز وجل: ﴿يَـٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ ٱلصِّيَامُ كَمَا كُتِبَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبْلِكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ﴾ قال: إنما فرض الله صيام شهر رمضان على الأنبياء دون الأمم ففضل به هذه الأمة وجعل صيامه فرضاً على رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) وعلى أمته.
thaqalaynSanad: My father (ra) narrated to us, saying that Saʿd b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, from al-Qāsim b. Muḥammad al-Iṣfahānī, from Sulaymān b. Dāwūd al-Munqarī, from Ḥafṣ b. Ghiyāth al-Nakhʿī, who narrates: “I heard Abā ʿAbd Allāh (as) saying:

Fasting has been prescribed for you—as it was for those before you—so perhaps you will become mindful of Allāh﴿?” [2:183], so he replied: “Allāh ordained fasting in the month of Ramaḍān only upon the Prophets, and not their respective communities as well. Thus, Allāh has favoured this community with it and made fasting a duty upon the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) and his community.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Al-Ḥasan b. Muḥammad b. Saʿīd al-Hāshimī narrated to us, saying that Furāt b. Ibrāhīm al-Kūfī narrated to him among others, saying that Muḥammad b. Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī—known as Abū ʿAlī al-Shāmī—narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. Saʿīd al-Zabarqānī narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd al-Wāḥid b. Ghiyāth narrated to him among others, saying that ʿĀṣim b. Sulaymān narrated to him among others, saying that Juwaybir narrated to him among others, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk, from Amīr al-Muʾminīn, ʿAlī b. Abī Ṭālib (as), who narrates: “The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) has said: “Shaʿbān is my month, and the month of Ramaḍān is the month of Allāh. So, for whomsoever fasts in my month, I shall serve as an intercessor for him on the Day of Reckoning. Whoever fasts in the month of Allāh (azwj), then Allāh shall relieve his loneliness in his grave, grant him companionship therein, and resurrect him from his grave, his face shining with white light, and give him the record of his deeds to take in his right hand, and eternal bliss in his left, until he is presented before his Lord (azwj), Who shall address him: “O’ My servant!,” so he will reply: “I am at Your call, o’ my Master!,” and Allāh will continue: “You fasted for My sake?,” so the man will respond: “Yes, o’ my Master!” So He (azwj) will say: “Take My servant by the hand until he is brought to Me,” so I shall bring him henceforth. I will say to him: “You fasted in my month?,” so he replies: “Yes,” and I will continue: “Today, I shall be your intercessor.” The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) then said: “Allāh (twt) will say: “Concerning My rights, I have devolved them to My servant. As for the rights of My creation, then whoever excuses him—this servant of Mine—then upon Me is compensating him until he is satisfied.” The Holy Prophet (sawa) then continued his narration: “I shall take him by the hand until I stop—with him—at the Bridge, finding it a slippery, treacherous passage whereupon the feet of the malefactors do not get to be firmly planted. I will, nevertheless, take him by the hand (and lead him there) until the Bridge-keeper says to me: “Who is this, o’ Messenger of Allāh?,” so I shall respond: “This is so-and-so, a person of my community. In worldly life, he had fasted in my month, seeking the fulfillment of my intercession, and he had also fasted in the month of his Lord, seeking the fulfillment of His promise.” Thus he shall be granted passage over the Bridge—with the extenuation of Allāh (azwj)—and we will carry on traveling until we stop before the gate to the two Paradisiacal realms. The gate will open for him, and Riḍwān shall say: “Our orders are that it will open, today, for you and for your community.” Amīr al-Muʾminīn (as) concluded: “I implore you to fast in the month of the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) so that he may serve as an intercessor for you, and to fast in the month of Allāh so that you may drink from the sealed nectar.”
arabicText: حدثنا الحسن بن محمد بن سعيد الهاشمي، قال: حدثنا فرات بن إبراهيم الكوفي، قال: حدثنا محمد بن أحمد بن علي الهمداني، قال: حدثنا الحسن علي بن المعروف بأبي علي الشامي، [1] قال: حدثنا عبد الله بن سعيد الزبرقاني، قال: حدثنا عبد الواحد بن غياث، قال: حدثنا عاصم بن سليمان، قال: حدثنا جويبر، عن الضحاك، عن أمير المؤمنين علي بن أبي طالب (عليه السلام)، قال: قال رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله): شعبان شهري وشهر رمضان شهر الله، فمن صام شهري كنت له شفيعاً يوم القيامة، ومن صام شهر الله عز وجل آنس الله وحشته في قبره ووصل وحدته وخرج من قبره مبيضاً وجهه وأخذ الكتاب بيمينه والخلد بيساره حتى يقف بين يدي ربه عز وجل، فيقول: عبدي، فيقول: لبيك سيدي، فيقول عز وجل: صمت لي؟ قال فيقول: نعم، يا سيدي، فيقول تبارك وتعالى: خذوا بيد عبدي حتى تأتوا به مني، فأوتي به فأقول له: صمت شهري؟ فيقول: نعم، فأقول: أنا أشفع لك اليوم، قال: فيقول الله تبارك وتعالى: أما حقوقي فقد تركتها لعبدي وأما حقوق خلقي فمن عفا عنه فعلي عوضه حتى يرضى. قال النبي (صلى الله عليه وآله): فآخذ بيده حتى انتهى به إلى الصراط فأجده دحضاً مزلقاً لا يثبت عليه أقدام الخاطئين، فآخذ بيده فيقول لي صاحب الصراط: من هذا يا رسول الله؟ فأقول: هذا فلان من أمتي كان قد صام بالدنيا شهري ابتغاء شفاعتي وصام شهر ربه ابتغاء وعده، فيجوز الصراط بعفو الله عز وجل حتى ينتهي إلى باب الجنتين فاستفتح له فيقول رضوان: لك أمرنا أن نفتح اليوم ولأمتك، قال: ثم قال أمير المؤمنين (عليه السلام): صوموا شهر رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يكن لكم شفيعاً، وصوموا شهر الله تشربوا من الرحيق المختوم.

Aḥmad b. ʿAlī al-Hamadānī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥasan b. ʿAlī—known as Abū ʿAlī al-Shāmī—narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAbd Allāh b. category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: The jurist, Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Aḥmadānī al-Aswarī, [1] narrated to us, saying that Makkī b. Aḥmad b. Saʿdawayh al-Barwāghī narrated to him among others, saying that the jurist Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Abū ʿAmrū Yaʿqūb b. Yūsuf al-Qazwīnī narrated to him among others—in Baghdad—saying that Abū’l-Qāsim b. al-Ḥakam al-ʿArī narrated to him among others, saying that Hāshim b. al-Walīd narrated to him among others, from Ḥammād b. Sulaymān al-Sadūsī, saying that the elder teknonymised as “Abū’l-Ḥasan” narrated to him among others, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Muzāḥim, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, that he heard the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) saying: “Verily! From year to year, Paradise is beautified and adorned to welcome the month of Ramaḍān. So, when it is the first night of the month of Ramaḍān, a scent emanates from beneath the Throne—which is called “al-Mutanazzah”—rustling the leaves of the trees of Paradise and the rings of its gates on its way, thereby making a sound of which there is no other more melodious than it. The celestial maidens (ḥūr al-ʿayn) shall adorn themselves and stand between the positions of honour in Heaven, calling out: “Is there anybody who would declare before Allāh (azwj) that he may take us in marriage?,” and then the angels shall exclaim: “O’ Riḍwān, what is this night?,” while he is chanting in praise. Then he will respond: “O’ winsome goodnesses! This is the first night of the month of Ramaḍān. The gates of the Paradisiacal realms have been opened for those who fasted from among the community of Muḥammad.” Allāh (azwj) will then say: “O’ Riḍwān! Open the gates of the Heavenly realms! O’ Mālik! Shut the gates of Hell to those who fasted and stood upright for prayer from among the community of Muḥammad. O’ Jibraʿīl! Descend to the Earth and inter the rebellious devils, shackle them with strong shackles and then cast them into the depths of the seas so that they will not cause disorder in the community of My beloved while they are fasting.” The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) continued his narration: “And in every night of the month of Ramaḍān, Allāh (azwj) bids His angels descend thrice, while Allāh (azwj) calls: “Is there any asker of a favour that I may give him that which he has asked for? Is there any repenter seeking My acceptance of his repentance? Is there any seeker of forgiveness to whom I may grant forgiveness? Who would grant a loan to the Unassessably Wealthy One Who is never in need, and the Loyal without wrongdoing?” Verily, every day of the month of Ramaḍān—at the time of breaking the fast—Allāh (twt) grants certain people freedom from the Fire. On the night and day of Friday, in every hour, He frees a million souls from the Fire, all of whom were otherwise condemned to punishment. On the last day of the month of Ramaḍān, He will absolve as many souls from perdition on that day as He has throughout the entire month, from its first to its last day. When the Night of Power arrives, Allāh (azwj) shall command Jibraʿīl to descend to the Earth with a host of angels accompanying him and a green banner, which he shall plant atop the Kaaba. Jibraʿīl has six hundred wings, two of which he does not unfurl except on the Night of Power—so he will spread them on that night, extending over the East and the West. Jibraʿīl (as) will then bid the angels disperse among this community so that they greet every sitting, standing, praying, and remembering person, shake their hands, and say “Āmīn” to their supplications until the break of dawn. When dawn breaks, Jibraʿīl will call out: “O’ assembly of angels, depart! Depart!” They will say: “O’ Jibraʿīl! What has Allāh decreed concerning the needs of the believers of Muḥammad’s (sawa) community?” He shall reply: “Verily, Allāh (azwj) has looked upon them and forgiven them this night—all of them—except for four.” It was asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh! Who are these four?” He replied: “A man who dies addicted to alcohol, one who is undutiful to his parents, one who severs ties of kinship, and one who harbours enmity.” It was asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is meant by one who harbours enmity?” He replied: “One who refuses to reconcile. The night before ʿĪd al-Fiṭr is called the Night of Reward. When morning arrives on the day of Fiṭr, Allāh (azwj) sends forth the angels to all lands, and they descend to the Earth, stopping at the entrances of alleyways and calling out with a voice heard by all creation—except humans and jinn—saying: “O’ community of Muḥammad, come forth to your Lord! A Noble Lord Who bestows generously and forgives greatly!” When the people emerge to proceed to their place of prayer, Allāh (azwj) shall say: “O’ My angels, what is the recompense of a worker who has fulfilled his task?” The angels shall reply: “O’ our God and Master! His recompense is that You, being true to Your promise, grant him his due reward.” He (azwj) shall say: “I bear witness before you, My angels, that I have made My pleasure and My forgiveness the reward for their fasting in the month of Ramaḍān and their standing in prayer.” Then He (jj) will say: “O’ My servants! Ask of Me, for by My Might and Majesty, you shall not ask Me for anything today—whether for your Hereafter or your worldly life—except that I shall grant it or take it into account for you. By My Might, I shall conceal your faults as long as you remain mindful of Me. By My Might, I shall neither disgrace nor expose you before the companions of eternity. Depart, for you are forgiven—you have pleased Me, and so I am pleased with you.” The angels will then ascend, rejoicing over what Allāh (azwj) has bestowed upon this community when they depart from the month of Ramaḍān.” Abū ʿAmrū al-Qazwīnī said: “Al-Ḥasan b. ʿUrfa al-ʿAbdī asked me about this narration in the year 46 AH, so I narrated it to him, and al-Ḥasan narrated it forth—from a certain man—from Qāsim b. al-Ḥakam al-ʿAranī.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبو الحسن علي بن عبد الله بن الأحمداني الأسواري الفقيه، قال: حدثنا مكّي بن أحمد بن سعدويه البروغي، قال: حدثنا أحمد بن عبد الله الفقيه، قال: حدثنا أبو عمرو يعقوب بن يوسف القزويني ببغداد، قال: أبو القاسم بن الحكم العري، قال: حدثنا هاشم بن الوليد، عن حماد بن سليمان السدوسي، قال: حدثنا شيخ يكنى أبا الحسن، عن الضحاك بن مزاحم، عن عبد الله بن عبّاس انه سمع رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله) يقول: إن الجنة لتحبر وتزين من الحول إلى الحول لدخول شهر رمضان فإذا كانت أول ليلة من شهر رمضان هبت ريح من تحت العرش يقال لها: المتنزّه يصفق ورق الأشجار من الجنة وحلق المصاريع فيسمع من ذلك طنين لم يسمع صوت بأحسن منه فتتزين الحور العين تقف بين شرف الجنة فينادين هل من خاطب إلى الله عز وجل فنتزوجه، ثم قالت الملائكة: يا رضوان ما هذه الليلة؟ فيلبيهن بالتلبية. ثم يقول: يا خيرات حسان هذه أول ليلة من شهر رمضان فتحت الجنان للصائمين من أمة محمد، ويقول الله عز وجل: يا رضوان افتح أبواب الجنان! يا مالك أغلق أبواب الجحيم عن الصائمين القائمين من أمة محمد! يا جبرئيل اهبط إلى الأرض فصفد مردة الشياطين وغلهم بالأغلال ثم اقذفهم في لجج البحار حتى لا يفسدوا في أمة حبيبي صيامهم. قال: وينزل الله عز وجل ملائكته في كل ليلة في شهر رمضان ثلاث مرات يقول الله عز وجل: هل من سائل فاعطيه سؤله؟ هل من تائب فأتوب عليه؟ هل من مستغفر فأغفر له، من يقرض الملي غيره المعدم والوفي غير الظلوم؟ فإن الله تبارك وتعالى في كل يوم من شهر رمضان عند الافطار عتيق من النار، فإذا كانت ليلة الجمعة ويوم الجمعة أعتق في كل ساعة منهما ألف ألف عتيق من النار كلهم قتد استوجبوا العذاب فإذا كان في آخر يوم من شهر رمضان أعتق في ذلك اليوم بعدد ما أعتق من أول الشهر إلى آخره، فإذا كان ليلة القدر أمر الله عز وجل جبرئيل فهبط في كوكبة من الملائكة إلى الأرض ومعه لواء أخضر فيركز اللواء على ظهر الكعبة وله ستمائة جناح منها جناحان لا ينشرهما الا في ليلة القدر فينشرهما في تلك الليلة فيتجاوز المشرق والمغرب، ويبث جبرئيل (عليه السلام) الملائكة في هذه الأمة فيسلمون على كل قائم وقاعد ومصل وذاكر ويصافحونهم ويؤمنون على دعائهم حتى يطلع الفجر فإذا طلع الفجر نادى جبرئيل: يا معشر الملائكة، الرحيل الرحيل! فيقولون: يا جبرئيل ما صنع الله في حوائج المؤمنين من أمة محمد؟ فيقول: إن الله عز وجل قد نظر إليهم في هذه الليلة وغفر لهم إلا أربعة، فقيل: يا رسول الله من هؤلاء الأربعة؟ قال: رجل مات مدمن خمر، وعاق والديه، وقاطع رحم، ومشاخن، قيل: يا رسول الله وما المشاخن؟ قال: هو المصارم. فإذا كانت ليلة الفطر سميت تلك الليلة ليلة الجائزة فإذا كانت غداة الفطرة بعث الله عز وجل الملائكة في كل البلاد فيهبطون إلى الأرض فيطوفون [على] إلى أفواه السكك فينادون بصوت يسمعه جميع من خلق الله إلا الجن والإنس، فيقولون: يا أمة محمد اخرجوا إلى ربكم رب كريم يعطي الجزيل ويغفر العظيم! فإذا برزوا إلى مصلاهم يقول الله عز وجل: يا ملائكتي ما جزاء الأجير إذا عمل عمله؟ فتقول الملائكة: إلهنا وسيدنا جزاؤه أن توفيه أجره، قال: فيقول عز وجل: فإني أشهدكم ملائكتي أني قد جعلت ثوابهم عن صيامهم شهر رمضان وقيامهم رضائي ومغفرتي، ويقول جل جلاله: يا عبادي سلوني فوعزتي وجلالي، لا تسألوني اليوم شيئاً في جمعكم لآخرتكم إلا أعطيتكم ولدنياكم إلا نظرت لكم وعزتي لأسترن عليكم عثراتكم ما رأيتموني وعزتي لا أخزينكم ولا أفضحنكم بين يدي أصحاب الخلود انصرفوا مغفوراً لكم قد أرضيتموني فرضيت عنكم، فتعرج الملائكة وتستبشر بما يعطي الله عز وجل هذه الأمة إذا أفطروا من شهر رمضان. قال أبو عمرو القزويني: سألني عن هذا الحديث الحسن بن عرفة العبدي سنة ست وأربعين، فحدثته به وكان الحسن يحدث عن رجل عن قاسم بن الحكم العرني.
thaqalaynSanad: The jurist, Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. al-Aḥmadānī al-Aswarī, [1] narrated to us, saying that Makkī b. Aḥmad b. Saʿdawayh al-Barwāghī narrated to him among others, saying that the jurist Aḥmad b. ʿAbd Allāh narrated to him among others, saying that Abū ʿAmrū Yaʿqūb b. Yūsuf al-Qazwīnī narrated to him among others—in Baghdad—saying that Abū’l-Qāsim b. al-Ḥakam al-ʿArī narrated to him among others, saying that Hāshim b. al-Walīd narrated to him among others, from Ḥammād b. Sulaymān al-Sadūsī, saying that the elder teknonymised as “Abū’l-Ḥasan” narrated to him among others, from al-Ḍaḥḥāk b. Muzāḥim, from ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAbbās, that he heard the Messenger of Allāh (sawa) saying:
thaqalaynMatn: “Verily! From year to year, Paradise is beautified and adorned to welcome the month of Ramaḍān. So, when it is the first night of the month of Ramaḍān, a scent emanates from beneath the Throne—which is called “al-Mutanazzah”—rustling the leaves of the trees of Paradise and the rings of its gates on its way, thereby making a sound of which there is no other more melodious than it. The celestial maidens (ḥūr al-ʿayn) shall adorn themselves and stand between the positions of honour in Heaven, calling out: “Is there anybody who would declare before Allāh (azwj) that he may take us in marriage?,” and then the angels shall exclaim: “O’ Riḍwān, what is this night?,” while he is chanting in praise. Then he will respond: “O’ winsome goodnesses! This is the first night of the month of Ramaḍān. The gates of the Paradisiacal realms have been opened for those who fasted from among the community of Muḥammad.” Allāh (azwj) will then say: “O’ Riḍwān! Open the gates of the Heavenly realms! O’ Mālik! Shut the gates of Hell to those who fasted and stood upright for prayer from among the community of Muḥammad. O’ Jibraʿīl! Descend to the Earth and inter the rebellious devils, shackle them with strong shackles and then cast them into the depths of the seas so that they will not cause disorder in the community of My beloved while they are fasting.” The Messenger of Allāh (sawa) continued his narration: “And in every night of the month of Ramaḍān, Allāh (azwj) bids His angels descend thrice, while Allāh (azwj) calls: “Is there any asker of a favour that I may give him that which he has asked for? Is there any repenter seeking My acceptance of his repentance? Is there any seeker of forgiveness to whom I may grant forgiveness? Who would grant a loan to the Unassessably Wealthy One Who is never in need, and the Loyal without wrongdoing?” Verily, every day of the month of Ramaḍān—at the time of breaking the fast—Allāh (twt) grants certain people freedom from the Fire. On the night and day of Friday, in every hour, He frees a million souls from the Fire, all of whom were otherwise condemned to punishment. On the last day of the month of Ramaḍān, He will absolve as many souls from perdition on that day as He has throughout the entire month, from its first to its last day. When the Night of Power arrives, Allāh (azwj) shall command Jibraʿīl to descend to the Earth with a host of angels accompanying him and a green banner, which he shall plant atop the Kaaba. Jibraʿīl has six hundred wings, two of which he does not unfurl except on the Night of Power—so he will spread them on that night, extending over the East and the West. Jibraʿīl (as) will then bid the angels disperse among this community so that they greet every sitting, standing, praying, and remembering person, shake their hands, and say “Āmīn” to their supplications until the break of dawn. When dawn breaks, Jibraʿīl will call out: “O’ assembly of angels, depart! Depart!” They will say: “O’ Jibraʿīl! What has Allāh decreed concerning the needs of the believers of Muḥammad’s (sawa) community?” He shall reply: “Verily, Allāh (azwj) has looked upon them and forgiven them this night—all of them—except for four.” It was asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh! Who are these four?” He replied: “A man who dies addicted to alcohol, one who is undutiful to his parents, one who severs ties of kinship, and one who harbours enmity.” It was asked: “O’ Messenger of Allāh, what is meant by one who harbours enmity?” He replied: “One who refuses to reconcile. The night before ʿĪd al-Fiṭr is called the Night of Reward. When morning arrives on the day of Fiṭr, Allāh (azwj) sends forth the angels to all lands, and they descend to the Earth, stopping at the entrances of alleyways and calling out with a voice heard by all creation—except humans and jinn—saying: “O’ community of Muḥammad, come forth to your Lord! A Noble Lord Who bestows generously and forgives greatly!” When the people emerge to proceed to their place of prayer, Allāh (azwj) shall say: “O’ My angels, what is the recompense of a worker who has fulfilled his task?” The angels shall reply: “O’ our God and Master! His recompense is that You, being true to Your promise, grant him his due reward.” He (azwj) shall say: “I bear witness before you, My angels, that I have made My pleasure and My forgiveness the reward for their fasting in the month of Ramaḍān and their standing in prayer.” Then He (jj) will say: “O’ My servants! Ask of Me, for by My Might and Majesty, you shall not ask Me for anything today—whether for your Hereafter or your worldly life—except that I shall grant it or take it into account for you. By My Might, I shall conceal your faults as long as you remain mindful of Me. By My Might, I shall neither disgrace nor expose you before the companions of eternity. Depart, for you are forgiven—you have pleased Me, and so I am pleased with you.” The angels will then ascend, rejoicing over what Allāh (azwj) has bestowed upon this community when they depart from the month of Ramaḍān.” Abū ʿAmrū al-Qazwīnī said: “Al-Ḥasan b. ʿUrfa al-ʿAbdī asked me about this narration in the year 46 AH, so I narrated it to him, and al-Ḥasan narrated it forth—from a certain man—from Qāsim b. al-Ḥakam al-ʿAranī.”

category: The Book of Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad al-Aswarī narrated to us, saying that Makkī b. Aḥmad b. Saʿdawayh al-Bardaʿī narrated to him among others, saying that Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm b. Saḥḥūn [1] informed him among others, saying that ʿAmrū b. Zabāl—Abū Ḥafṣ—narrated to him among others, saying (that he narrated it from) Khātim b. ʿUbayda, who said that ʿAlī b. Ḥijr narrated it to him among others, saying that Yūsuf b. Ziyād narrated to him among others, from Hammām b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī b. Zayd b. Jadhʿān, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, from Salmān al-Fārisī, who reported that the Messenger of Allāh (sws) delivered a sermon—to a congregation that included him—on the last day of Shaʿbān, saying: “O’ people! Verily, an exalted and blessed month has cast its shadow over you, a month in which there is a night greater than a thousand months. Allāh has made fasting in this month an obligation. Whoever seeks nearness (to Allāh) in it through a single virtue shall be as one who fulfilled an obligation in any other month, and whoever fulfills an obligation in this month shall be as one who fulfilled seventy obligations in any other. It is the month of patience—and patience’s reward is Paradise—and the month of compassion, and the month in which the sustenance of the believers is increased. Whoever provides a fasting person with something to break his fast, it shall be an expiation for his sins and a means of freeing his neck from the Fire, without diminishing anything from the reward of the fasting person.” It was said: “O’ Messenger of Allāh! Not all of us can find something with which to provide a fasting person to break his fast!” So he (sws) replied: “Allāh grants this reward to one who provides a fasting person with no more than a sip of milk or a drink of water. Whoever satiates a fasting person, Allāh shall quench his thirst with a drink from my Basin, after which he shall never thirst again until he enters Paradise. This is a month whose beginning is mercy, whose middle is forgiveness, and whose end is absolution from Perdition. Whoever lightens the burden of his servant in this month, Allāh shall forgive him and grant him freedom from the Fire. So, increase in four characteristics during this month: two by which you shall please your Lord, and two which you cannot do without. As for the two by which you shall please your Lord, they are the testimony that there is no god but Allāh and seeking His forgiveness; and as for the two which you cannot do without, they are your asking Allāh for Paradise and your seeking His protection from the Fire.”
arabicText: حدثنا أبو الحسن بن علي بن عبد الله بن أحمد الأسوري، قال: حدثنا مكّي بن أحمد بن سعدويه البردعي، قال: أخبرنا أبو إسحاق إبراهيم بن سححون، قال: حدثنا عمرو بن زبال أبو حفص، قال: خاتم بن عبيدة، قال: حدثنا علي بن حجر، قال: حدثنا يوسف بن زياد، عن همام بن يحيى، عن علي بن زيد بن جذعان، عن سعيد بن المسيّب، عن سلمان الفارسي، قال: خطبنا رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) في آخر يوم شعبان، فقال: أيها الناس فإنه قد أظلكم شهر عظيم شهر مبارك شهر فيه ليلة خير من الف شهر جعل الله صيامه فريضة من تقرب فيه بخصلة من خصال الخير كان كمن أدى فريضة فيما سواه، ومن أدى فيه فريضة كمن أدى سبعين فريضة فيما سواه [وهو] فهو شهر الصبر، والصبر ثوابه الجنة، وشهر المواساة وشهر يزاد فيه الرزق للمؤمنين، من فطر فيه صائماً كان مغفرة لذنوبه وعتق رقبة من النار من غير أن ينتقص من أجره شيئاً. قيل: يا رسول الله ليس كلنا يجد ما يفطر به الصائم، فقال (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم): يعطي الله هذا الثواب من فطر صائماً على قطرة من لبن أو شربة من ماء ومن أشبع صائماً سقاه الله من حوضه شربة لا يظمأ بعده حتى يدخل الجنة، وهو شهر أوله رحمة وأوسطه مغفرة وآخره عتق من النار، ومن خفف فيه عن مملوكه غفر الله له وأعتقه من النار، فاستكثروا فيه من أربع خصال خصلتين ترضون بهما ربكم وخصلتين لأغنى بكم عنهما فأما الخصلتان اللتان ترضون بهما ربكم فشهادة أن لا إله إلا الله وتستغفرونه، وأما اللتان لا غنى بكم عنهما فتسألون الله الجنة وتتعوذون به من النار.
thaqalaynSanad: Abū’l-Ḥasan ʿAlī b. ʿAbd Allāh b. Aḥmad al-Aswarī narrated to us, saying that Makkī b. Aḥmad b. Saʿdawayh al-Bardaʿī narrated to him among others, saying that Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm b. Saḥḥūn [1] informed him among others, saying that ʿAmrū b. Zabāl—Abū Ḥafṣ—narrated to him among others, saying (that he narrated it from) Khātim b. ʿUbayda, who said that ʿAlī b. Ḥijr narrated it to him among others, saying that Yūsuf b. Ziyād narrated to him among others, from Hammām b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī b. Zayd b. Jadhʿān, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, from Salmān al-Fārisī, who reported that the Messenger of Allāh (sws) delivered a sermon—to a congregation that included him—on the last day of Shaʿbān, saying:

chapter: Merits of the Month of Ramaḍān
author: Shaykh Muḥammad b. ʿAlī al-Ṣaduq
englishText: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥāmid [or Khālid] narrated to us this narration, saying that Ḥāmid b. Muḥammad al-Raqqā al-Harawī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. Ibn Idrīs [1] narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. Ḥijr narrated to him among others, saying that Yūsuf b. Ziyād narrated to him among others, from Hammām b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī b. Zayd, from Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib, from Salmān, who said: “The Messenger of Allāh (sws) delivered to us a sermon at the end of Shaʿbān…,” and he mentioned the narration like it, in the same manner.
arabicText: وحدثنا بهذا الحديث أبو محمد عبد الله بن حامد [خالد]، قال: حدثنا حامد بن محمد الرقّاء الهروي، قال: حدثنا الحسين بن ابن إدريس، قال: حدثنا علي بن حجر، قال: حدثنا يوسف بن زياد، عن همام بن يحيى، عن علي بن زيد، عن سعيد بن المسيّب، عن سلمان، قال: خطبنا رسول الله (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) في آخر شعبان وذكر الحديث مثله سواء.
thaqalaynSanad: Abū Muḥammad ʿAbd Allāh b. Ḥāmid [or Khālid] narrated to us this narration, saying that Ḥāmid b. Muḥammad al-Raqqā al-Harawī narrated to him among others, saying that al-Ḥusayn b. Ibn Idrīs [1] narrated to him among others, saying that ʿAlī b. Ḥijr narrated to him among others, saying that Yūsuf b. Ziyād narrated to him among others, from Hammām b. Yaḥyā, from ʿAlī b.
